alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->Invalid parameters
alarms.long_description: The ACU4 Controller holds invalid parameters. The ACU4 Controller cannot start its application without the correct parameters.
alarms.cause: The alarm is caused from the ACU4 Controller automatically loads the wrong parameter set after a replacement of the ACU4 Controller.
alarms.effect: The behaviour of the application in the ACU4 Controller is not correct. The precise effect of this situation is unknown and care should be taken.
alarms.suggested_action: If the involved ACU4 Controller just have been replaced, wait for the automatic preparation to complete. If this takes more than 10 minutes, the LED colour signalling for fault indication should be inspected. If this proves unhelpful, reset the ACU4 Controller unit. If it still does not help, contact MAN-ES.

- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->24V Power Supervision->Noise Detector->Electrical noise detected
alarms.long_description: Electrical noise has been detected in the ECS system
alarms.cause:
- One or more ECS components has intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's ground, or
- ECS system has been subjected to electrical noise from an external source

NOTE: 
Unless IRM module is used, the location of a ECS component causing the alarm is NOT limited to the ACU4 Controller on which the alarm has appeared.
alarms.effect:
No immediate effect
The fault can generate other consequential alarms in the ECS system, e.g. 
- Exh. Valve Closed Position Changed
- Exh. Valve closing/opening too fast/slow (4 alarms)
- Illegal ELFI/FIVA Position
- ELFI/FIVA Feedback Signal Failure

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Noise pulse counter by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Cabling, sensors, actuators, Controllers for loose connections or intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakages/short circuits to ground.

To locate an intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's ground:
1.Stop engine or reduce rpm to slow down level
2. Set the ACU4 Controller in TEST MODE by pressing MPC mode button on MOP Maintenance -> System view
I/O. This will stop the controllers normal function.
3. Disconnect connections one at a time (except for the power cable), and after each disconnection observe if
increase in noise pulse counter has stopped
4. If increase has stopped, the cable, sensor or actuator with loose connections or intermittent and/or
oscillating electric leakages/short circuits to ground, has been located
5.Revert to basic electrical trouble shooting to repair
6.Set the ACU4 Controller in NORNAL MODE by pressing MPC mode button on MOP Maintenance -> System view I/O

NOTE: 
If a CCU is disconnected or stopped for more than 20 minutes, establishing of emergency lubrication to the affected cylinder is recommended, by fitting of backup lubrication cables from ECU.

alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->24V Power Supervision->PD ch 1 Fuse failure
alarms.long_description: Power failure on ACU4 power distribution module, terminal X1.
alarms.cause:
- Overcurrent.
- Short circuit.
- Faulty sensor(s)/actuator(s).

If alarm occurs together with "PD input power detected", input voltage is detected on power distribution module, terminal X1.
alarms.effect: No power is supplied from terminal X1.\n\nIf alarm occurs together with "PD input power detected", see effect from "PD input power detected" alarm info.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cabling
- Connected sensor(s)/actuator(s) for malfunction(s) (too high current load).

Reset the fuse on terminal X1 via the display on the CPU module:
- <Right> key to enter "Service"
- <Down> key to enter "Fuse, DO & AO"
- <Enter> key enter "Reactivate all fuses after error"
- <Enter> key to re-activate fuses

Note: If alarm occurs together with "PD input power detected", see suggested action from "PD input power detected" alarm info.

alarms.cause: Incorrect setup of the network switches.\nDefect switch or port on switch.\nDefect CPU module
alarms.effect: The nodes are not able to synchronize with the PTP master.\nMay reduce engine performance

   3) replace the CPU module

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Disabled Channel
alarms.cause: I/O channel has been disabled.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action: Please check cables and HW connected to the I/O\nReenable the channel via the UI on the CPU module, once the problem has been fixed.\nReplace the module if the problem persists or if no problem external to the module is found.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU4->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Module unavail.
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

alarms.cause:
- Cabling failure, or
- Sensor failure, or
- Supervision resistor across the switch is missing, or 
- ACU4 Controller input channel failure
alarms.effect:
Reduced system performance.
Reduced supervision.

NOTE 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cabling
- Sensor
- Supervision resistor 
- ACU4 Controller input channel: 'Maintenance' -> 'System View I/O Test'

If the problem persists: Replace the corresponding module on ACU4

- Manual circulation pump shut off valves

alarms.effect: - LDCL Pump will not be allowed to start until inlet pressure is normal.\n- LDCL system is stopped, but should go back to Automatic when problem is fixed.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check that LDCL pump inlet shut-off valve is open\n- Check that jacket water outlet valve is open\n- Check that pump inlet pressure sensor is working correctly

alarms.cause: Differential pressure is low
alarms.effect: Insufficient cooling water flow. \n If differential pressure decreases further, a slowdown will be requested.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check the following:

- If any maintenance has been carried out on the engine please ensure that if any orifices have been removed those have been re-installed.
- Please compare the differential pressure with local pressure gauges.

- All the cooling water valves on the engine are in the correct position: - inlet/outlet of the liners - inlet/outlet for the cylinder cover/exhaust valves - drain valves etc.

alarms.cause:
- Cabling failure, or
- Sensor failure, or
- Supervision resistor across the switch is missing, or 
- ACU4 Controller input channel failure
alarms.effect: Reduced supervision. May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:

- Supervision resistor 
- ACU4 Controller input channel: 'Maintenance' -> 'System View I/O Test'

If the problem persists: Replace the corresponding module on ACU4

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU4->PIFIW->IO Configuration->AI,1848,Diesel Flow [kg/h]->1848-Diesel Flow [kg/h]-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU4->PIFIW->PIFIW Control->Mix System->Production Rate Deviation->Production Rate Too Low
alarms.long_description: PIFIW Production Rate FB is too low compared to SP
alarms.cause: Insufficient flow control on PIFIW unit
alarms.effect: If the engine emulsion fuel consumption is higher than the production rate FB over a longer period, then the level in the emulsion tank will decrease too much and PIFIW will shut down
alarms.suggested_action: - Check the water and diesel flow on the PIFIW unit and in CoCoS to find out which flows that is insufficient

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU4->PIFIW->PIFIW Control->Mix System->Production Rate Deviation->Production Rate Too High
alarms.long_description: PIFIW Production Rate FB is too high compared to SP
alarms.cause: Insufficient flow control on PIFIW unit
alarms.effect: The PIFIW system will continue to run
alarms.suggested_action: Check the water and diesel flow on the PIFIW unit and in CoCoS to find out which flows that is insufficient.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU4->PIFIW->PIFIW Control->Mix System->Emulsifier Flow Deviation->Emulsifier Flow Too Low
alarms.long_description: The emulsifier flow deviates too much from the set point
alarms.cause: - The emulsifier tank is empty\n- The emulsifier pump is not working properly
alarms.effect: The diesel and water will not mix as intended which can result in damaging components on the engine
alarms.suggested_action: - If the emulsifier tank is empty, stop the dual fuel system. When the dual fuel sytem is stopped, fill the emulsifier tank while trying to reduce the amount of foam created. Drain all air trapped in the emulsifier pipes. The dual fuel system with PIFIW can hereafter be started again\n- If the emulsifier tank is full, check the emulsifier pump

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU4->PIFIW->PIFIW Control->Emulsion Tank->Drain Valve->Drain Valve Failure
alarms.long_description: Drain Valve position deviates from commanded position
alarms.cause: - Valve failure, or\n- Feedback failure, or\n- Cabling failure (Opened FB, Closed FB, Open Command)
alarms.effect: - PIFIW shutdown\n- DF Shutdown
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Valve
- Valve feedback
- Valve cabling (Opened FB, Closed FB, Open Command)

Further troubleshooting.
1. Operate valve by changing ACU4 Controller mode to test. Avoid doing this while the engine is running.
2. Observe feedback during valve operation

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU4->PIFIW->PIFIW Control->Emulsion Tank->Emulsion Tank Level Too Low
alarms.long_description: PIFIW Emulsion Tank level is too low
alarms.cause: - Leakage from pipe or tank \n- Failing Drain Valve \n- Failing Level Transmitter
alarms.effect: - PIFIW shutdown\n- DF Shutdown \n- Possible emulsion leakage to Engine Room
alarms.suggested_action: - Check Emulsion Tank \n- Check Drain Valve \n- Check Cables

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU4->PIFIW->PIFIW Control->Emulsion Tank->Emulsion Tank Level Too High
alarms.long_description: PIFIW Emulsion tank level is too high
alarms.cause: - Malfunctioning Mix System \n- Signal or cabling failure \n- Failing Level Transmitter
alarms.effect: No immediate effect
alarms.suggested_action: - Check alarm on PIFIW Mix System\n- Check cabling

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU4->PIFIW->PIFIW Control->Fuel Booster->Remote Local-Fail
alarms.cause: - PIFIW Fuel Booster Pump is manually set to 'Local' \n- PIFIW Fuel Booster Pump failure
alarms.effect: - PIFIW shutdown\n- DF Shutdown
alarms.suggested_action: Investigate PIFIW Fuel Booster Pump

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU4->PIFIW->PIFIW Control->Fuel Booster->Filter dp Too High
alarms.long_description: Differential pressure across the PIFIW Fuel Booster filter is too high
alarms.cause: - PIFIW Fuel Booster filter is clogged\n- Fuel Filter p-In sensor is malfunctioning\n- Fuel Filter p-Out sensor is malfunctioning
alarms.effect: No immediate effect
alarms.suggested_action: - Clean or change the clogged PIFIW Fuel Booster filter\n- Check cabling\n- Replace malfunctioning sensor

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU4->PIFIW->PIFIW Control->Fuel Booster->Fuel Pump Deviating
alarms.long_description: PIFIW Fuel Booster Pump feedback deviates from setpoint
alarms.cause: - PIFIW Fuel Booster Pump failure\n- Signal or cabling failure on the PIFIW Fuel Booster Pump feedback or setpoint
alarms.effect: - PIFIW shutdown\n- DF Shutdown
alarms.suggested_action: - Investigate PIFIW Fuel Booster Pump\n- Check cabling\n- Replace malfunctioning sensor

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU4->PIFIW->PIFIW Control->Fuel Booster->Fuel Pressure Too Low
alarms.long_description: Fuel Filter p-Out (1844) measueres too low pressure for second fuel running
alarms.cause: - PIFIW Fuel Booster Pump failure\n- Sensor failure\n- Leakage
alarms.effect: - PIFIW shutdown\n- DF Shutdown
alarms.suggested_action: - Check PIFIW Fuel Booster Pump\n- Check Filter p-Out Sensor\n- Check for Leakage

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU4->PIFIW->PIFIW Control->State Machine Supervision->Draining Timeout
alarms.long_description: Draining the Emulsion Tank did not finish within the allowed time
alarms.cause: - Malfunctioning Drain Valve\n- Blockage in the Drain Pipes or Tank\n- Failure in ECS control system
alarms.effect: - PIFIW shutdown\n- DF Shutdown
alarms.suggested_action: - Check Drain Valve\n- Check Pipes and Drain tank

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU4->PIFIW->PIFIW Control->State Machine Supervision->Fill Emulsion Tank Timeout
alarms.long_description: Filling the Emulsion Tank did not finish within the allowed time
alarms.cause: - Malfunctioning Mix System\n- Failure in ECS control system
alarms.effect: - PIFIW shutdown\n- DF Shutdown
alarms.suggested_action: - Check Mix System

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU4->PIFIW->PIFIW Control->State Machine Supervision->Fill Engine Timeout
alarms.long_description: Filling Engine did not finish within the allowed time
alarms.cause: - Malfunctioning Fuel Pump\n- Leakage\n- Failure in ECS control system
alarms.effect: - PIFIW shutdown\n- DF Shutdown
alarms.suggested_action: - Check Fuel Pump\n- Check for Leakage

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU4->PIFIW->PIFIW Control->State Machine Supervision->Circulation Timeout
alarms.long_description: PIFIW has been in Circulation State for longer than allowed
alarms.cause: - PIFIW has been in Circulation State for longer than allowed"\n- Failure in ECS control system
alarms.effect: - PIFIW shutdown\n- DF Shutdown
alarms.suggested_action: - Select Tier III on MOP and PIFIW will mix a new batch and start again

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU4->PIFIW->PIFIW Control->Forced PIFIW Failure
alarms.cause: Parameter with ID=ACU4-PFIWCFail is set to Yes
alarms.effect: - PIFIW shutdown\n- DF Shutdown
alarms.suggested_action: Set Parameter with ID=ACU4-PFIWCFail to No

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU4->PIFIW->PIFIW Monitoring->PIFIW and LGIMW Switch->PIFIW or LGIMW not Connected
alarms.long_description: PIFIW or LGIMW is not properly connected
alarms.cause: - Both PIFIW and LGIMW are connected\n- Or both PIFIW and LGIMW are not connected\n- Or signal or cabling failure on LGIMW or PIFIW
alarms.effect: - PIFIW or LGIMW Shutdown\n- DF Shutdown
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check cabling of PIFIW and LGIMW
- If PIFIW must be connected check that LGIMW is not connected 
- If LGIMW must be connected check that PIFIW is not connected 
- Replace malfunctioning sensors (PIFIW sensor: XC1846) (LGIMW sensor: XC1845)

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Module unavail.
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->I/O Configuration->ACU Commands->No Commands from ECU A
alarms.long_description: No control values from ECU A received over the control network
alarms.cause: - ECU failure, or\n- Control network performance loss
alarms.effect: If "No commands received... " from one ECU only: No effect.\nIf "No commands received ..." from both ECUs: No HPS or blower control available on this ACU
alarms.suggested_action: Check network status.\n\nIf "No command received.." from both ECU's: Manual start of startup pump and aux. blower is required from local control panel.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->I/O Configuration->ACU Commands->No Commands from ECU B
alarms.long_description: No control values from ECU B received over the control network
alarms.cause: - ECU failure, or\n- Control network performance loss
alarms.effect: If "No commands received... " from one ECU only: No effect.\nIf "No commands received ..." from both ECUs: No HPS or blower control available on this ACU
alarms.suggested_action: Check network status.\n\nIf "No command received.." from both ECU's: Manual start of startup pump and aux. blower is required from local control panel.

alarms.synopsis: No SCR Data Received from ECU A
alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->I/O Configuration->ERCS Interface->SCR System->SCR Telegram Data from ECUs->No SCR Data Received from ECU A
alarms.long_description: ACU1 Controller did not receive the SCR data network telegram from the ECU.
alarms.cause: - ECUA is not in normal mode\n- ECUA failure \n- Network problems from ECUA
alarms.effect: - If telegrams are missing from one ECU Redundancy reduced.\n- The ACU1 Controller will continue normal operation, based on telegrams from redundant ECU.\n- If telegrams are missing from both ECUs SCR operation and Tier III mode is not possible.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check :
- Network status on MOP maintenance screen.
- Network cabling, include terminating resistors.
- Ground failure.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->I/O Configuration->ERCS Interface->EGR System->Telegram Data from EGRCU->No Telegram Received from EGRCU

alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- If the EGRCU is working correctly.\n- Both network connections (network A and B) between ACU1 Controller and EGRCU.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU->I/O Configuration->DI,1224-1,Prop Valve Amp.->1224-1-Prop Valve Amp.-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->Blower Ctrl. 1->Blower 1 Ctrl Failed
alarms.long_description: Electric motor cannot be controlled by the engine control system
alarms.cause:
- Electric motor switchboard is off or manually set to 'Local', or
- Electric motor switch board failure, or
- Switchboard feedback failure, or
- Cabling failure
alarms.effect: If the failure is in the feedback part only: No effect\nElse: No ECS control of electric motor
alarms.suggested_action:
1. Check that the operation control switch at the switchboard is set to ''Remote'
2. Check switchboard, main breaker and overcurrent protection relay
3. Check cabling

If all is OK: Set switch to 'Off' and wait a few seconds. 
Reset switch to ''Remote'

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->Hydraulic Power Supply->Swashplate pump ctrl->Pump ctrl failure
alarms.long_description: The ACU1 Controller cannot control swash plate pump for HPS
alarms.cause:
- No position feedback signal from proportional valve, or 
- No swash plate position feedback signal, or 
- Proportional valve amplifier failure, or 
- Mechanical pump failure
alarms.effect:
ECS will attempt to deliver full flow:
- Full flow ahead, if engine runs ahead
- Full flow astern, if engine runs astern

If two or more pumps fail:
Engine may not be able to run astern.

In case of mechanical pump failure: ECS may deliver low or no flow to the HPS.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check cabling to and from: 
- Proportional valve
- Proportional valve amplifier
- LVDT amplifier 
- ACU1 Controller 
    
Check pump and proportional valve

Go to 'Auxiliaries' -> 'Hydraulic System' -> 'Failed pump' to reset failure state.

Further troubleshooting:
1. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HPS'
2. Test failing pump swashplate operation.
3. Compare signals from failing pump to signals from a well functioning pump.

alarms.cause: - Failure on air supply to valves.\n- Valve failure.\n- Signal or cabling failure on the valve feedback or setpoint.

alarms.suggested_action: Investigate Compressor Cut Out Valve and EGR Blower Bypass Valve.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->TC Cut Out->Supervision->TC Cut Out/In Operation Failed
alarms.long_description: Turbocharger cut out/in operation has failed to reach a state of either all TCCO valves open or all TCCO valves closed.
alarms.cause: - Failure on air supply to valves.\n- Valve failure.\n- Signal or cabling failure on the valve feedback or setpoint.
alarms.effect: - Compressor is cut in while Turbine is cut out. Turbocharger will run in reverse and might get damaged.\n- ECS changes to Turbocharger Cut Out state and sets all TCCO valve setpoints to close.
alarms.suggested_action: - Keep engine load low to protect turbocharger.\n- Investigate Turbine Cut Out Valve, Compressor Cut Out Valve and EGR Blower Bypass Valve.

alarms.effect: - Turbine is cut in while compressor might be cut out. Risk of turbine overspeed!\n- Cancellable slowdown activated.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->TC Cut Out->Supervision->TCV Closed in TCCI State

alarms.cause: - Failure on air supply to valves.\n- Valve failure.\n- Signal or cabling failure on the valve feedback or setpoint.
alarms.effect: - Turbine cut out while the compressor might be cut in.\n- Risk of turbocharger running in reverse, possibly damaging the turbocharger!\n- Cancellable slowdown activated.
alarms.suggested_action: - Slow down engine.\n- Investigate Turbine Cut Out Valve.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->TC Cut Out->Supervision->CCV Closed in TCCI State

alarms.effect: - Compressor is cut out while turbine might be cut in. Risk of turbocharger overspeed!\n- Cancellable slowdown activated.
alarms.suggested_action: - Slow down engine.\n- Investigate Compressor Cut Out Valve.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->TC Cut Out->Supervision->BBV Closed in TCCI State

alarms.suggested_action: - Slow down engine.\n- Investigate EGR Blower Bypass Valve.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->TC Cut Out->Supervision->TCCO Valve Position Invalid

alarms.cause:
- Valve is manually being operated.
- Failure on air supply to valves.
- Valve failure.
- Signal or cabling failure on the valve feedback.
alarms.effect: Risk of turbocharger running in reverse or overspeeding.
alarms.suggested_action: - Finish manual valve operation.\n- Slow down engine.\n- Investigate Turbocharger Cut Out valves.

alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- TCV SEQ valve
- CCV SEQ valve
- Turbocharger

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->Seq TC Cut Out->Failure Handling->TC Speed Monitoring->TC Speed Too High (Cut Out)
alarms.long_description: Turbocharger speed is too high while turbocharger is cut out
alarms.cause:
- TCV SEQ valve failure
- CCV SEQ valve failure
- for EGR engine: BBV SEQ valve failure
- Failure on air supply to valves
- Signal or cabling failure
- Sipart power failure
- Magnetic positioner sensor failure
alarms.effect: Valves will open and the turbocharger will be cut in. Seq TC will go into failure mode
alarms.suggested_action:
- Slowdown engine
- Check valves
- Check Siparts
- Check turbocharger
When problem is fixed: Go into manual mode and cut out/in turbocharger to be able to enter automatic mode

alarms.suggested_action: - Check the Seq TC Air system, or\n- Check for major leakages

alarms.cause: - Sequential TC cut out valve failure\n- Failure in the EGR system (if installed)
alarms.effect: - Turbocharger cut out/in cancelled by ECS\n- Engine load will ramp up to initial value before load limitation was activated\n- Seq TC will go into failure mode
alarms.suggested_action: Check other alarms. When problem is fixed: Go into manual mode and cut out/in turbocharger to be able to enter automatic mode

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->Seq TC Cut Out->Failure Handling->Failure TCCI request

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->CR Supply Control->Pressure Controller->CR Index Control Failure
alarms.long_description: CR Pressure 8056 out of range\nor CR Pressure Setpoint from ECU not valid
alarms.cause: CR Pressure sensor failure or\n-Network failure
alarms.effect: - CR pump index is forced to 100%\n- Combivalve may be activated
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n-CR pressure sensor cabling\n-Network connection ECU ->ACU

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->CR Supply Control->Pressure Controller->CR Index High
alarms.long_description: CR Pump index is at near 100%
alarms.cause: - Leakage in Rail or Pipes\n- Failing pump
alarms.effect: -If pump capacity is insufficient, it can cause the fuel pressure to drop.\n-This can ultimately cause a reduction of the load or a shutdown
alarms.suggested_action: - Check of pipes and drains\n- Check CR pump\n- Check CR pump drive (VLT)

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->CR Supply Control->Pump Motor Control->CR Pump Motor Ctrl Failed
alarms.long_description: Electric motor cannot be controlled by the engine control system
alarms.cause:
- Electric motor switchboard is off or manually set to 'Local', or
- Electric motor switch board failure, or
- Switchboard feedback failure, or
- Cabling failure
alarms.effect: If the failure is in the feedback part only: No effect\nElse: No ECS control of electric motor
alarms.suggested_action:
1. Check that the operation control switch at the switchboard is set to 'Remote'
2. Check switchboard, main breaker and overcurrent protection relay
3. Check cabling
If all is OK: Set switch to 'Off' and wait a few seconds.
Reset switch to 'Remote'
NOTE:
If a pump is actually running, but ECS running signal is both missing, engine start will be blocked (start blocked).

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->CR Supply Control->Leakage Supervision->CR Pipe Leakage Detected
alarms.long_description: CR Fuel leakage from inner to outer pipe
alarms.cause: CR Fuel oil detected in outer pipe. i.e. the inner pipe leaks
alarms.effect: - Fuel Oil leak may affect the Pressure and the available engine load.\n- Reduced Pressure can lead to shutdown
alarms.suggested_action: Find and repair the leak

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->CR Supply Control->Leakage Supervision->CR Pump Leakage Detected
alarms.long_description: CR Fuel leakage in drain from Rail or CR Pump

alarms.effect: Continuous operation may result in larger leakage.
alarms.suggested_action: Find and repair the leak

alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Valve
- Valve feedback
- Actuator air supply
- Valve cabling

Further troubleshooting after end of dual fuel operation:
1. Operate valve by changing ACU1 Controller mode to test.
2. Observe feedback during valve operation

alarms.cause:
-Turbocharger worn or fouled.
- High back pressure.
- High pressure drop across air cooler. 
- Extreme high ambient temperature
alarms.effect: Alarm
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Turbocharger for wear and fouling exhaust gas side (TC rotor wear / Nozzle ring fouling). Air side for fouling (Air filter / compressor).
- Scavenging air cooler water side for calcium build up and air side for fouling. 
- Exhaust gas boiler for blocked pipes and fouling

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->Axial Vibration Monitoring->AV Peak to Peak High
alarms.cause: Axial vibration damper performance is reduced, possible causes: worn or damaged sealing rings in damper housing.\n- Reduced lubrication oil pressure. \n- Lubrication oil aeration or unequally cylinder combustion.
alarms.effect: Alarm
alarms.suggested_action:
Change speed to range where there is no alarm and check the AVD asap. 
- Reduced lubrication oil pressure. 
- Lubrication oil aeration or unequally cylinder combustion .
- Damper piston (crankshaft) or damper housing damaged, or defective torsional vibration damper (if applied)

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->Axial Vibration Monitoring->AV Peak to Peak [SLD]
alarms.cause: Axial vibration damper performance is reduced .
alarms.effect: Main engine slow down.
alarms.suggested_action: -Engine running is not recommended in this condition. \n- Change speed to range where there is no alarm and check the AVD asap \n- Possible causes worn or damaged sealing rings in damper housing, reduced lubrication oil pressure, lubrication oil aeration or unequally cylinder combustion, damper piston (crankshaft) or damper housing damaged, or defective torsional vibration damper (if applied) other unspecified engine damages.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->EGB Control->Pscav Supervision->Too High Pscav
alarms.long_description: Scavenging air pressure (Pscav) is too high
alarms.cause: - bypass valve is closed AND current engine load is high, or\n- Pscav measurement failure
alarms.effect: Bypass valve automatically moves to open position until pressure is reduced.
alarms.suggested_action:
Switch to manual control

NOTE
If engine load above 75% is required, open bypass valve mechanically or via MOP

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->EGB Control->EGB in Manual Mode
alarms.long_description: Bypass valve control has switched to manual
alarms.cause: User has switched to manual control on MOP
alarms.effect: No automatic bypass valve position control
alarms.suggested_action: Switch back to automatic control as soon as manual operation is completed

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->EGB Control->EGB Deviation
alarms.long_description: Exhaust Gas Bypass (EGB) valve position deviates from the set point
alarms.cause:
- Exhaust Gas Bypass (EGB) valve stiction, or
- Exhaust Gas Bypass (EGB) actuator failure, or
- Cable failure, or
- MPC failure
alarms.effect: If valve is stuck in closed or partly closed position, keep the engine load below 75%
alarms.suggested_action:
Power off the Exhaust Gas Bypass (EGB) valve actuator and power it on again
If the problem persists:
-Check cabling and mechanics
-Recalibrate Exhaust Gas Bypass (EGB) valve actuator

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->EGB Control->High Scavenge Air Pressure [SLD]
alarms.long_description: Scavenging air pressure (Pscav) is too high
alarms.cause: - EGB valve is too closed for the current engine load, or\n- Measurement equipment failure, or\n- Turbocharger failure
alarms.effect: Slowdown request is issued to the safety system.
alarms.suggested_action:
1. Keep engine load below 75%
2. Reset slowdown
3. Set the EGB valve to fully open
4. Resume normal engine operation.

If the problem persists, check:
- Pscav measurement equipment. Compare to other Pscav measurements. 
- Mechanical position of EGB valve

If the problem persists: Open bypass valve by local control or mechanically (refer to actuator manual).

alarms.synopsis: TC Overspeed Proxy Has Bad Status
alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->EGB Control->TC Overspeed Proxy Has Bad Status
alarms.long_description: There is bad status on the TC overspeeding signal sent from EICUB to ACU3 with proxy
alarms.cause: - The signal has bad status\n- Network failure
alarms.effect: EGB will not open if TC overspeeding occurs
alarms.suggested_action: - Check MOP Maintenance page for disconnected units and missing communication \n- Check network cabling

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->TC Lube Oil Inlet Pressure Control->TC Lube Oil Inlet Pres. Supervision->Reduced Pressure Too High
alarms.long_description: TC Lube Oil Inlet Pressure is too high while pressure reduction is active.
alarms.cause: - TC Lube Oil Inlet Pressure Reduction Valve is not closing correctly.\n- TC Lube Oil Inlet Pressure Reduction Flow Control Valve not calibrated correctly.\n- Faulty pressure sensor.
alarms.effect: Prolonged high pressure may result in Lube Oil leaking into TC and exhaust receiver.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check TC Lube Oil Inlet Pressure Reduction Valve, and its cabling.\n- Check TC Lube Oil Inlet Pressure Reduction Flow Control Valve.\n- Check TC Lube Oil Inlet Pressure Transducer, and its cabling.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->TC Lube Oil Inlet Pressure Control->TC Lube Oil Inlet Pres. Supervision->Reduced Pressure Too Low
alarms.long_description: TC Lube Oil Inlet Pressure is too low while pressure reduction is active.
alarms.cause: - TC Lube Oil Inlet Pressure Reduction Flow Control Valve not calibrated correctly.\n- Leakage in TC Lybe Oil Supply System.\n- Faulty pressure sensor.
alarms.effect: Insufficient lube oil being delivered to TC which may result in damage to TC.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check TC Lube Oil Inlet Pressure Reduction Flow Control Valve.\n- Check for leaks.\n- Check TC Lube Oil Inlet Pressure Transducer, and its cabling.

alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU->I/O Configuration->DO,2111-B,Engine Not Ready->2111-B-Engine Not Ready-Module unavail.
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU->I/O Configuration->DO,1170-B,Start Air Dist. Pos.->1170-B-Start Air Dist. Pos.-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.effect: Signal value is outside the valid range and cannot be measured.\nMay reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action: Please check cabling and/or sensor.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU->I/O Configuration->AI,8605-3,Scav.Air before AC->8605-3-Scav.Air before AC-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU->I/O Configuration->AI,8605-3,Scav.Air before AC->8605-3-Scav.Air before AC-Module unavail.
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU->I/O Configuration->AI,8605-3,Scav.Air before AC->Warning: Physical input override

alarms.cause: Manual I/O channel overriding for testing an input channel is active.
alarms.effect:

Overriding:
 - Can cause hazardous situation and engine damage if used incorrectly!
 - Can cause or prevent alarms.
 - Can cause or prevent engine shut down/slow down.
 - Can cause or prevent duel SF stop or SF shut down.
alarms.suggested_action: Disable I/O channel override immediately after testing.\nLocate the overridden channel in the Maintenance -> system I/O view page. Manual channel override is indicated with a "!" in a yellow triangle in the Status column.

alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU->I/O Configuration->DO,1170-NA,Start Air Dist. Pos.->1170-NA-Start Air Dist. Pos.-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU->I/O Configuration->DO,1170-NA,Start Air Dist. Pos.->1170-NA-Start Air Dist. Pos.-Disabled Channel
alarms.cause: I/O channel has been disabled.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action: Please check cables and HW connected to the I/O\nReenable the channel via the UI on the CPU module, once the problem has been fixed.\nReplace the module if the problem persists or if no problem external to the module is found.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU->Monitoring Signals->Lub.Oil Press LPS->Lub.Oil Press LPS Low
alarms.long_description: Lubrication oil pressure after LPS de-aeration too low (PT1230)
alarms.cause: LPS booster pump failure . \n- LPS booster pump leakage . \n-  LPS oil pressure sensor failure
alarms.effect: Alarm
alarms.suggested_action: Check : \n- LPS booster pump system. \n-Pressure sensor PT1230

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU->Monitoring Signals->Lub.Oil Temp Engine->Lub.Oil Temp Engine High
alarms.long_description: Lubrication oil temperature at engine inlet too high (TI/TE1310)
alarms.cause: - Oil coolers failure. \n- Oil coolers water supply failure.
alarms.effect: Alarm
alarms.suggested_action: Check : \n- Lubrication oil coolers cooling water supply . \n- Temperature sensor TI/TE1310

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU->Monitoring Signals->Lub.Oil Temp Engine->Lub.Oil Temp Engine [SLD]
alarms.long_description: Lubrication oil temperature at engine inlet too high (TI/TE1310)- slowdown
alarms.cause: - Oil coolers failure. \n- Oil coolers water supply failure.
alarms.effect: Slowdown Request
alarms.suggested_action: Check : \n- Lubrication oil coolers cooling water supply . \n- Temperature sensor TI/TE1310

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU->Monitoring Signals->Lub.Oil Diff Filt->dp across filter too high
alarms.long_description: HPS main filter pressure drop too high (PDS1231)
alarms.cause: Difference pressure measured across HPS main filter is too high. \n- Filter element may be clogged causing flow restriction
alarms.effect: Risk of contamination in hydraulic oil .\n- Particle contamination can cause abrupt control valve failure and will increased wear.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check difference pressure by inspecting mechanical reading on filter unit  
- Inspect HPS main filter for contamination and track reason for contamination. 
- Check oil sample for contamination using particle counting and investigate type of contamination material . 
- Increase purifier to 24/7 operation to remove impurities .
- Use Super Fine Filter (SFF) to clean hydraulic oil.

alarms.synopsis: dp across SFF filter too high
alarms.data_tree_path: ACU->Monitoring Signals->Auto Filter Alarm->dp across SFF filter too high
alarms.long_description: PDS1241 Pressure differnece across SFF filter too high
alarms.cause:
Depending on the type of filter, this could indicate :
-Main filter clogged (backflushing unsuccessful). 
- Filter control failure .
- SFF filter clogged
alarms.effect: Alarm
alarms.suggested_action: Check the filter control for local indications (consult makers manual) . \n- Inspect the filter elements triggering the alarm

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Shutdown
alarms.long_description: Shutdown has been ordered.\n\nThis is a group alarm caused by a shutdown order from the safety system. Other alarms in the group are raised as a consequence of this condition. To view all alarms in this group: Press +/- at the bottom of the MOP screen.
alarms.cause:
1. Requested by engine control system due to: 
    - Hydraulic leakages from HPS, or
    - System oil inlet pressure too low, or
    - Hydraulic high pressure too low

2. Ordered by safety system
alarms.effect: The engine stops.\nFuel injection stops immediately.
alarms.suggested_action:
If the shutdown was requested by the engine control system, check:
- Hydraulic leakages from HPS
- System oil inlet pressure 
- Hydraulic high pressure

alarms.data_tree_path: Shutdown alarm missing
alarms.long_description: Shutdown has been ordered. One or more controllers have not yet confirmed shutdown.\n\nThis is an alarm caused by a shutdown order from the safety system and one or more controllers do not report shutdown.
alarms.cause: - Shutdown feedback signal from affected controller delayed or missing, or\n- No shutdown signal from safety system
alarms.effect: One or more controllers may try to keep engine running because it may not have received the shut down signal from the safety system.
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Controllers, that have not confirmed the shutdown. Power off, if necessary.\n- Cabling and signal from safety system to CCU Controllers Shut Down Safety System and ECU Controllers Shut Down.

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Tacho set A failure
alarms.long_description: Abnormal tacho set A signals on multiple CCUs/ECUs .\n\nThis group alarm is caused by multiple 'Tacho set A failure' alarms. Other alarms in the group are raised as a consequence of this condition. To view the alarms in the group: Press +/- at the bottom of the MOP screen.
alarms.cause:
- Cabling failure (loose connection etc.), or
- Turning wheel marker sensor failure, or
- Encoder failure, or
- Tacho amplifier A failure, or
- Sensor support console failure, or
- Power failure (ECUA powers tacho set A)

If trigger ring is fitted, this alarm may be caused by:
- Trigger/marker ring is damaged, or
- Trigger/marker sensor failure
alarms.effect: The CCUs/ECUs has switched to tacho set B. \nRedundancy reduced.
alarms.suggested_action:
If only one ECU or CCU reports failure: Check Connector for Marker Master - Tacho input set A, Marker Slave - Tacho input set A, Quadrature 1 - Tacho input set A and Quadrature 2 - Tacho input set A on failing unit.
If OK: Replace ECU or CCU

If all CCUs and ECUs report tacho A failure, check tacho signals on maintenance screen and power to tacho amplifier TCA-A: 
  1. Check power on the tacho amplifier TSA-A connector J5 pin (J,A) J=24V A=0V.
  2. Turn the engine minimum one revolution (by turning gear) 
  3. On failing ECU or CCU maintenance screen: Check that Marker Master - Tacho input set A, Marker Slave - Tacho input set A, Quadrature 1 - Tacho input set A and Quadrature 2 - Tacho input set A toggle correctly between true and false    
      Marker Master - Tacho input set A and Marker Slave - Tacho input set A: twice per revolution 
      Quadrature 1 - Tacho input set A and Quadrature 2 - Tacho input set A: multiple times per revolution (360) 

Perform tacho test on MOP:
Go to Maintenance  -> Function Test -> Tacho 
Follow tacho test instructions

Trace the error by following the signal from :
    Encoder and/or turning wheel sensor
       ->Amplifier (TSA-A)
       ->TIU A (supplying power to TSA-A from Terminal X8 (D,A) D=24V A=0V)

If trigger ring is fitted, check:
     a. Trigger/marker ring
     b. Trigger/marker sensor

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Delta Tacho B too big
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Delta Tacho B too big
alarms.long_description: Abnormal angle difference between tacho system A and B\n\nThis group alarm is caused by 'Delta Tacho B too big'. To view all alarms in the group: Press +/- at the bottom of the MOP screen.
alarms.cause: The angle between tacho set A and B marker signal exceeds the limit.
alarms.effect: If the system switches from tacho set A to B, maximum pressure deviation may occur.
alarms.suggested_action:
If the alarm 'Tacho set A failure' or 'Tacho set B failure' is active: Ignore this alarm. 

If this alarm is the only tacho alarm:
- Check and adjust Pmax. 
- At first opportunity: 
    1. Inspect the mechanical condition of the encoders.

If this alarm is the only tacho alarm:

- At first opportunity: 
    1. Inspect the mechanical condition of the encoders. 
    2. Readjust the encoders
    3. Perform tacho test on MOP:
        Go to 'Maintenance ' -> 'Function Test' -> 'Tacho' 
        Follow tacho test instructions

NOTE
If encoder A is readjusted or replaced: Perform PMI measurement, and restore tacho offset settings according to 0-diagram

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Marker A input slip

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: ELFI/FIVA feedback failure (CCU1) [SLD]

- Internal ELFI/FIVA-feedback failure.

- Frozen IO Detected

No fuel injection

- No exhaust valve operation 
- Slowdown is requested
alarms.suggested_action:
Check ELFI/FIVA feedback cabling. 

Go to 'Engine' -> 'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' -> 'HCU Status and Reset' to reset failing unit 

Further troubleshooting:
1. Stop the engine at first opportunity

3. Test failing unit's injection and exhaust valve operation.

If the problem persists replace or exchange, one part at a time: 
- ELFI/FIVA valve
- ELFI/FIVA cabling
- CCU

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Illegal fuel plunger movement (CCU1) [SLD]
alarms.long_description:
The fuel plunger has made an illegal movement. 
Risk of untimed fuel injection.

This group alarm is caused by 'No cylinder lubrication', reported by both EICU A and EICU B. To view all alarms in the group: Press +/- at the bottom of the MOP screen.
alarms.cause: - Plunger position sensor or cable failure, or\n- ELFI / FIVA valve failure, or\n- CCU failure
alarms.effect:
No fuel injection due to risk of untimed fuel injection.

For FIVA installations:
- No exhaust valve operation 
- Slowdown is requested
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- CCU1 Controller Fuel plunger position sensor status
- Fuel plunger position sensor and cabling.

If the sensor is replaced, go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Function Test' to recalibrate the sensor. 

Reactivate fuel injection. Go to 'Engine' ->'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' -> 'HCU Status and Reset' to reset failing unit. 
Do not reactivate fuel injection until the cylinder unit is considered to be OK.

Further troubleshooting: 
1. Stop the engine at first opportunity. 
2. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU'
3. Test failing unit's fuel plunger operation

If the problem persists, replace or exchange, one part at a time: 
- Fuel plunger position sensor 
- Fuel plunger sensor cabling  
- ELFI / FIVA valve
- CCU

NOTE
Alarm can be overridden by invalidating CCU1 Controller FO Pump Plunger Position and reactivating fuel injection on 'Maintenance' -> 'System View I/O Test'

- Fuel plunger position sensor and cabling.

If the sensor is replaced, go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Function Test' to recalibrate the sensor. 

Reactivate fuel injection. Go to 'Engine' ->'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' -> 'HCU Status and Reset' to reset failing unit. 
Do not reactivate fuel injection until the cylinder unit is considered to be OK.

Further troubleshooting: 
1. Stop the engine at first opportunity. 
2. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU'
3. Test failing unit's fuel plunger operation

If the problem persists, replace or exchange, one part at a time: 
- Fuel plunger position sensor 
- Fuel plunger sensor cabling  
- ELFI / FIVA valve
- CCU

Alarm can be overridden by invalidating CCU12 Controller FO Pump Plunger Position and reactivating fuel injection on 'Maintenance' -> 'System View I/O Test'

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: FIVA Amplifier Thermal Protection Active (CCU1) [SLD]
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: FIVA Amplifier Thermal Protection Active (CCU1) [SLD]
alarms.long_description: Amplifier has shut down due to too high FIVA current consumption\n\nThis group alarm is raised because Amplifier has reached the current limit. Other alarms in the group are raised as a consequence of this condition. To view all alarms in this group: Press +/- at the bottom of the MOP screen.
alarms.cause:
- FIVA failure, or 
- Cabling failure, or 
- Amplifier failure, or
- CCU fuse (F9) for amplifier is blown
alarms.effect: No fuel injection. \nNo exhaust valve operation. \nSlowdown is requested
alarms.suggested_action:
1. Check FIVA cabling
2. Stop the engine at first opportunity 
3. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU' 
4. Test failing unit's injection and exhaust valve operation 
5. Compare signals from failing unit to signals from a well functioning unit
6. Reduce 'Chief Index limit [%]' first and then Re-enable HCU:
   
   'Chief Limiters' -> 'Chief Index limit [%]' below 40 %.
   'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' -> 'HCU Status and reset' Reset 'Fault' button.
   Set again 'Chief Index limit [%]' to the same value as before. 

If the problem persists replace or exchange, one part at a time: 
- FIVA valve
- FIVA amplifier 
- FIVA cabling
- CCU

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Hydraulic pressure sensor ACU1 deviates
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Hydraulic pressure sensor ACU1 deviates
alarms.long_description: Hydraulic oil pressure sensor (1201-x) on this ACU deviates from the hydraulic oil pressure sensors on the two other ACUs.
alarms.cause:
a. Hydraulic pump failure, or
b. Sensor failure, or
c. ECU Controller failure, or 
d. Cable failure
alarms.effect:
If a:
Engine performance may be reduced due to reduced hydraulic capacity.

If b, c, and d:

alarms.suggested_action:

d. Sensor

1. Reduce engine load until stable engine performance is achieved
2. Check other alarms
3. Check pump and pump drive shaft

If b, c, or d:
Repair or replace failing part

alarms.long_description: Swash plate follow pump set points deviate too much from the model curve
alarms.cause:
- Hydraulic leak, or 
- Swash plate pump failure (hydraulic failure, broken pump shaft etc.), or
- Proportional valve failure, or
- ECU Controller failure, or
- Proportional valve amplifier failure (if fitted)

NOTE
This alarm may occur during wind milling. In this case, this alarm can be ignored.
alarms.effect: Engine performance and HPS pressure may be reduced.\nEngine will shut down, if the HPS pressure drops below shutdown level.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Hydraulic system for leaks 
- Swash plate pumps for mechanical failures
- Proportional valves

Perform HPS function test on MOP: 'Maintenance' -> 'Function Test'

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Changing pressure controling pump
alarms.cause:
- No position feedback signal from proportional valve, or 
- No swash plate position feedback signal, or 
- Proportional valve amplifier failure, or 
- Mechanical pump failure
alarms.effect:
ECS will attempt to deliver full flow:
- Full flow ahead, if engine runs ahead
- Full flow astern, if engine runs astern

If two or more pumps fail:
Engine may not be able to run astern.

In case of mechanical pump failure: ECS may deliver low or no flow to the HPS.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check cabling to and from: 
- Proportional valve
- Proportional valve amplifier
- LVDT amplifier 
- ECU Controller 
    
Check pump and proportional valve

Go to 'Auxiliaries' -> 'Hydraulic System' -> 'Failed pump' to reset failure state.

Further troubleshooting:
1. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HPS'
2. Test failing pump swashplate operation.
3. Compare signals from failing pump to signals from a well functioning pump.

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Torque limiter cancelled
alarms.long_description:
Swash plate pump torque limit is cancelled.

NOTE
NEVER cancel pump torque limiter, unless one or more swash plate pumps do not deliver sufficient flow.
alarms.cause: Pump torque restriction has been cancelled manually (Chief-level access required).
alarms.effect: No pump torque restrictions
alarms.suggested_action: Enable the torque limiter as soon as the problem is  solved.

alarms.suggested_action: Switch back to automatic control as soon as manual operation is completed

- Engine driven pump

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Standby pump started
alarms.long_description: The Standby startup pump has been started
alarms.cause:
Master start-up cannot build hydraulic pressure within time limits or cannot maintain hydraulic pressure, because of: 

- HPS electric driven start-up pump failure, or 
- Hydraulic leakage
alarms.effect: Engine may be unable to start due to low hydraulic pressure
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- If both start-up pumps are running 
- Local pressure gauge on start-up pumps
- For hydraulic leakages

If hydraulic pressure can be maintained when both pumps are running, switch master pump: 'Auxiliaries' -> 'Hydraulic System'

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Hydraulic pressure deviates from setpoint
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Hydraulic pressure deviates from setpoint
alarms.long_description: The hydraulic pressure deviates from the hydraulic pressure set point calculated by the engine control system
alarms.cause: - Hydraulic system leakage, or\n- Engine driven pump failure, or\n- Engine driven pump calibration failure
alarms.effect: If the hydraulic pressure is lower than the ECS computed setpoint and it continues to decrease, the hydraulic pumps cannot deliver enough oil to maintain the pressure. If the pressure drops below 145 - 150 bar, the ECS is likely to carry out a shutdown. If the pressure is too high, it could lead to increased injection pressure.
alarms.suggested_action:
Reduce engine load until stable engine performance is achieved.

Check:
- Hydraulic system for leaks
- Engine driven pump

If engine has only 2 engine driven pumps and the pressure is too high, then manually open relief valve pos 307 to reduce pressure to 225 bar equal to the setting of pressure reduction valve pos. 308.

If the problem persists: Recalibrate engine driven pump on MOP

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Pump inlet pressure low
alarms.long_description: Lubrication oil inlet  pressure is low.
alarms.cause: - Sensor failure, or\n- Lubrication oil supply pump(s) not running, or \n- Inlet valve closed
alarms.effect:
No effect.

NOTE
If system oil pressure drops below shutdown level: 
Engine control system will request shutdown.
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Inlet pressure sensors \n- Lubrication oil supply system(pumps, valves, etc)

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Pump inlet pressure shutdown level
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Pump inlet pressure shutdown level
alarms.long_description: Lubrication oil inlet  pressure is below shutdown level.
alarms.cause: - Failing pressure sensors, or\n- Lubrication oil supply pump(s) not running, or \n- Inlet valve closed
alarms.effect: Engine control system has requested a non-cancellable shutdown to protect the HPS pumps.
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Inlet pressure sensors \n- Lubrication oil supply system(pumps, valves, etc)

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: No pump inlet sensors
alarms.cause: Sensors out of signal range or cabling is malfunctioning
alarms.effect: Engine will shut down
alarms.suggested_action: Inspect sensors and their cabling according to electrical wiring diagram

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Hydraulic pressure shutdown level
alarms.long_description: Hydraulic oil pressure below shutdown level
alarms.cause: - Failing hydraulic oil supply, or\n- Leakage in hydraulic oil distribution system, or\n- Failing hydraulic oil pressure sensors
alarms.effect: Engine will shut down.\nIt will not be possible to start engine with too low hydraulic oil supply pressure.
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Hydraulic oil supply system.\n- Hydraulic oil pressure sensors.

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Low Hydraulic Pressure
alarms.long_description: Maximum allowed fuel index is reduced due to insufficient hydraulic pressure
alarms.cause: - Pump failure, or \n- Hydraulic leakage, or\n- Bypass valve failure
alarms.effect: - Engine load may be reduced.\n- Unstable speed and fuel index. \n- Too low pressure will cause shutdown.
alarms.suggested_action:
To avoid unstable engine performance: Reduce engine load

Check for: 
- Hydraulic pump related alarms 
- Hydraulic leakages 
- Failing bypass valves

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: StartUP pump cmd state deviation
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: StartUP pump cmd state deviation
alarms.long_description: ECU A and ECU B are generating differing output values
alarms.cause:
Deviation between redundant input signals:
- to ECU A and ECU B 
OR 
- to ACU 1, 2 and 3 
OR
- from RCS
alarms.effect: Redundancy reduced
alarms.suggested_action:
Restart the engine to reset the alarm

If the problem persists, check:
- ECU cabling 
- ACU cabling
- RCS signals

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Running Failed
alarms.cause: - Sudden torque increase at low engine speed, or\n- Fuel starvation, or\n- Engine speed too low
alarms.effect: Engine does not run.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check: 
- Fuel oil supply system
- Fuel related alarms, if any

If all OK: Restart the engine

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Starting Failed
alarms.cause: - Starting air system failure, or\n- Torque too high, or \n- No fuel injection
alarms.effect: Engine did not start.\nAutomatic starting sequence has finished.\nManual restart is required.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Starting air system
- Fuel oil supply system

Restart the engine

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Turning Failed
alarms.long_description: Engine slow turning attempt failed\nEngine was not turned sufficiently
alarms.cause: - Starting air system failure, or\n- ECUB is controlling
alarms.effect: Engine may not be able to start.\nSlow-turning valve is not wired to ECUB and Engine start that require slow-turning will fail.
alarms.suggested_action:
1. Check ECUA is controlling
2. Check slow turning valve
3. Turn engine by turning gear to a different position
4. Retry manual slow turn before new engine start

If the problem persists, check:
- Start air pressure
- Starting air pilot valves
- Starting valves

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Manual blower operation demanded
alarms.cause: Operator has commanded manual blower operation.
alarms.effect: Engine cannot be started from bridge control station. \nBlowers switch to manual operation. All blowers are operated manually from MOP.
alarms.suggested_action: Switch back to automatic control as soon as manual operation is completed

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Insufficient blowers
alarms.long_description: Insufficient auxiliary blower capacity\n\nThis group alarm is raised because both ECU A and ECU B report, that 'Insufficient blowers capacity' has occurred. To view all alarms in this group: Press +/- at the bottom of the MOP screen.
alarms.cause: Less than half of the installed blowers are running.
alarms.effect:
Engine cannot be started from bridge control station.

NOTE
If 'Start' is initiated from ECR or LOP, engine will attempt to start even if no blowers are running.
alarms.suggested_action: 1. Check that the operation control switch at the switchboard is set to 'Remote'\n2. Check switchboard, main breaker and overcurrent protection relay\n3. Check cabling

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Start air pressure low
alarms.long_description: Start air pressure is too low
alarms.cause: - Air pressure in starting air tank is too low, or \n- Starting air supply valve is closed, or\n- Major starting air leakage
alarms.effect: Engine cannot be started from bridge.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Starting air system
- Starting air supply valve 

Engine start can be executed from ECR or LOP.

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Control air pressure low
alarms.long_description: Control air pressure is too low
alarms.cause: - Air pressure is too low, or \n- Control air supply valve is closed, or\n- Major control air leakage
alarms.effect: Engine is not ready.\nEngine may start, but performance will be severely affected.
alarms.suggested_action: Check the control air system

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Local Control Take Command Active
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Local Control Take Command Active
alarms.cause: 'Forced take control' button has been pressed on LOP
alarms.effect: The other control stations cannot take over engine control
alarms.suggested_action: To release engine control from LOP, deactivate 'Forced take control' button on LOP

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Air spring supply press low
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Air spring supply press low
alarms.cause: - Air pressure is too low, or\n- Air spring supply valve is closed, or\n- Major air spring supply leakage
alarms.effect: - Exhaust valve closing too slow\n- Exhaust valve lift too high with risk of mechanical failure
alarms.suggested_action: Check the air spring supply system

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Hydraulic HP Pump Failed on ACU1
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Hydraulic HP Pump Failed on ACU1
alarms.long_description: Hydraulic high pressure pump does not work correctly
alarms.cause: - Hydraulic pump failure, or\n- EICU Controller not running in normal mode, or \n- Network failure
alarms.effect:
Swash plate moves to fail safe position (maximum flow in ahead direction) 

Running ahead: 
No effect on engine performance.
Hydraulic pressure may increase. 

Running astern: 
Reversing the engine may not be possible due to insufficient hydraulic pressure.
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Other alarms to locate the root cause for the pump alarms\n- That the EICU Controller is in normal running mode

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Hydraulic HP Pump Failed on ACU3
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Hydraulic HP Pump Failed on ACU3
alarms.long_description: Hydraulic high pressure pump does not work correctly
alarms.cause: - Hydraulic pump failure, or\n- EICU Controller not running in normal mode, or \n- Network failure
alarms.effect:
Swash plate moves to fail safe position (maximum flow in ahead direction) 

Running ahead: 
No effect on engine performance.
Hydraulic pressure may increase. 

Running astern: 
Reversing the engine may not be possible due to insufficient hydraulic pressure.
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Other alarms to locate the root cause for the pump alarms\n- That the EICU Controller is in normal running mode

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: No Ctrl Station Selected
alarms.long_description: Inconsistent control station selection.\nNone or multiple control stations requested.
alarms.cause: - RCS and/or  RCS connection failure, or\n- Cabling failure
alarms.effect: - Engine control station is retained at current location.\n- Change of control station is only possible with "forced take".
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- RCS and connection to ECS
- Cabling

If problem persists:
- Restart EICU

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: ECR Control Station Forced
alarms.long_description: Engine control forced to ECR control station.
alarms.cause: ECR 'forced take' activated.
alarms.effect: Engine manoeuvre place is switched to ECR control station.\nOnly LOP 'forced take' can override this command.
alarms.suggested_action: No action

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Bridge Control Station Forced
alarms.long_description: Engine control forced to Bridge control station.
alarms.cause: Bridge 'forced take' activated.
alarms.effect: Engine manoeuvre place is switched to Bridge control station.
alarms.suggested_action: No action

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Handle Stop and Stop Switch Deviation
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Handle Stop and Stop Switch Deviation
alarms.long_description: The ECS (Engine Control System) has detected that the Handle Stop position and Stop Switch Position does not match the expected at the current selected control station.\n\nThis group alarm is raised because both EICU A and EICU B report, that the "Handle Stop position and Stop Switch Position" does not match. To view all alarms in this group: Press +/- at the bottom of the MOP screen.
alarms.cause:
- Stop switch or signal failure, or
- Analog handle or signal failure, or
- Analog handle stop is ON and Stop Switch is OFF, or
- Analog handle stop is OFF and Stop Switch is ON

Note: Analog handle Stop is ON  when handle speed set is zero RPM!
alarms.effect: Engine start can not be performed from current control station.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Analog handle signal and stop switch signal at current control station
- Stop switch
- Analog handle signal and calibration

To start engine: Change control station and activate engine start.

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Too many HP Pump Failures
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Too many HP Pump Failures
alarms.long_description: Two or more high pressure pumps are failing
alarms.cause:
More than one high pressure pump cannot be controlled.

NOTE
If more than 3 pumps are installed, pump 4 and 5 are controlled by the ECUs
alarms.effect: - High pressure pumps move to fail safe position (maximum flow in ahead direction)\n- Reversing the engine may not be possible due to insufficient hydraulic pressure
alarms.suggested_action:
Check other alarms to locate the root cause for the pump alarms

NOTE
NEVER ignore this alarm. Safe critical issues may arise!

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: In Barred Range Alarm
alarms.long_description: The actual speed has been in the barred speed range for too long.
alarms.cause: Actual engine speed deviate from speed set.
alarms.effect: No effect
alarms.suggested_action: Adjust speed set to move actual engine speed outside barred range.

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: In Barred Range Alarm

alarms.cause: Actual engine speed deviate from speed set.
alarms.effect: No effect
alarms.suggested_action: Adjust speed set to move actual engine speed outside barred range.

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Shop Test Mode Active
alarms.cause: Shop Test Mode can be toggled on/off from the ECT application. When it is toggled on this alarm is active.
alarms.effect:
The following changes are in effect to allow necessary shop test trials to be carried out:
1: Max Engine Speed has been increased from 105% to 110% MCR
2: Overspeed protection limit change from 106% and 108% MCR to 110% MCR
3: P-scav and Torque limiters have been cancelled
4: Chief index limiter has been raised from 110% to 120%
5: The load program has been disabled
6: Chief Max Speed parameter has been disabled

Changes 1 and 3 are only in effect when ECR is the active control station.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- EICU cabling

Reselect Shop Test Mode or Not Shop Test Mode on the ECT screen

If the problem persists:
- Restart either EICU A or EICU B when convenient

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Cyl 1. No Cylinder lubrication
alarms.long_description: No cylinder lubrication\n\nThis group alarm is caused by 'No cylinder lubrication', reported by both EICU A and EICU B. To view all alarms in the group: Press +/- at the bottom of the MOP screen.
alarms.cause: CCU 1 is not connected to the Network
alarms.effect: - No lubrication oil is injected\n- Slowdown is requested
alarms.suggested_action:
Check CCU1 Controller mode status
If in test or configuration mode: Restart in normal mode
If no mode is visible: Wait for CCU1 Controller to finish restart
If the problem persists: Replace CCU1 Controller

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: PMS (SG): Wait for Conditions
alarms.long_description: Time out while waiting for shaft generator engaging.
alarms.cause: The engine speed has been outside the acceptable range for connecting the shaft generator (SG) for too long after a SG connect request.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect.\nNote: Running in barred range may damage the engine.
alarms.suggested_action: Adjust speed set to be in the shaft generator (SG) speed range to make the PTO connect the SG or choose not to connect the SG

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: PMS (SG): Disconnection Fail
alarms.long_description: Time out while waiting for a shaft generator disengaging.
alarms.cause: - Disconnection of SG failure (or too long duration) , or\n- Cabling failure
alarms.effect: Engine control system will issue a cancellable shutdown request.
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Shaft generator connection status\n- Cabling to shaft generator

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: PMS (SG): Speed Outside Range
alarms.long_description: Actual speed exceeds the acceptable shaft generator speed range
alarms.cause: Current speed set outside legal range when shaft generator is engaged.
alarms.effect: Shaft generator is requested to disengage.
alarms.suggested_action: Adjust speed set inside legal shaft generator speed range.

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: PMS (WHR): Wait for Conditions
alarms.long_description: Time out while waiting for WHR system engaging.
alarms.cause: The engine speed has been outside the acceptable range for connecting the waste heat recovery system (WHR) for too long after a WHR connect request.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect.\nNote: Running in barred range may damage the engine.
alarms.suggested_action: Adjust speed set to be in the WHR speed range to make the PMS connect the WHR or choose not to connect the WHR

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: PMS (WHR): Disconnection Fail
alarms.long_description: Time out while waiting for a Waste heat recovery (WHR) disengaging.
alarms.cause: - Disconnection of WHR failure (or too long duration) , or\n- Cabling failure
alarms.effect: Engine control system will issue a cancellable shutdown request.
alarms.suggested_action: Adjust speed set to be in the WHR speed range to make the PMS connect the WHR or choose not to connect the WHR

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: PMS (WHR): Speed Outside Range

alarms.cause: Current speed set outside legal range when WHR is engaged.
alarms.effect: WHR is requested to disengage.
alarms.suggested_action: Adjust speed set inside legal WHR speed range.

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Global parameter inconsistency
alarms.long_description: EICU Controller parameter deviation. One or more parameters, the system expects to have the same value, differ.
alarms.cause: - If a user has adjusted a parameter at the MOP, one or more units have not received or accepted the change.\n- ERCS configuration error.
alarms.effect: - Engine performance may be affected.\n- Redundancy may be reduced.
alarms.suggested_action: Check that all controllers are in normal running mode.\n\nIf any parameter has been adjusted recently, repeat the adjustment.

- Pcomp/Pscav offset adjustments

WARNING! (GI engines)

Go to 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Gas Block'.

alarms.long_description: Cylinder expansion pressure is lower than expected
alarms.cause:
- Missing fuel oil injection, or
- Missing second fuel injection, or
- Misfiring, or
- Lower calorific value of sec fuel is too low, or
- Cylinder pressure sensor failure

Missing SF injection can be caused by:
- ELGI/ELFI-L valve failure, or
- Second fuel injection valve failure, or
- ELWI/ELBI valve failure
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel shutdown\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events'
- Alarms on MOP
- Fuel plunger timing and movement. Go to: 'MOP B' -> 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU Events'. 
- Look for ELFI enable signal on 'HCU Events'. 

Check on PMI:
- Cylinder pressure sensor signal. 
- Observe other alarms that might be the cause of the shutdown. Investigate the different possible scenarios

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Cyl. Pressure Rise Too Fast - SF Shutdown
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Cyl. Pressure Rise Too Fast - SF Shutdown
alarms.long_description: Cylinder pressure rise is too fast
alarms.cause: - Missing pilot oil injection resulting in late and hard ignition of second fuel, or\n- Seal oil leakage, or\n- GI engines: ELGI valve stuck in open position
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel shutdown
- Engine operation on fuel oil
- Second fuel blocked

WARNING! (GI engines)
Ignoring an ELGI valve stuck in open position will result in damage to SF injection valve, causing it to leak.

Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.

WARNING! (GI engines)
If second fuel pressure curve is abnormal (injection starts early when WV is activated or pressure drop is higher than normal), do not attempt to restart dual fuel operation, before engine has been stopped and gas block troubleshooting is completed. Go to 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Gas Block'.

Reference is made to circular letter or instruction manual showing pressure curves from typical failure situation.

If second fuel pressure curves are normal, check fuel plunger stroke measurements on CoCoS and go to 'Engine' -> 'Process Adjustment' -> 'Pilot Oil Profile' and increase offset on cylinder.

LGI engines
Check fuel plunger stroke measurements on CoCoS and go to 'Engine' -> 'Process Adjustment' -> 'Pilot Oil Profile' and increase offset on cylinder.

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: CYL1: No telegram from CCU
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: CYL1: No telegram from CCU
alarms.long_description: SCSU did not receive a telegram network message from CCU.\n\nTelegram is sent from CCU once per revolution, after receiving fuel telegram, and contains information about engine speed, fuel indexes and injection timing etc.
alarms.cause:
If SCSU reports this alarm continuously:
- CCU failure

If SCSU reports this alarm randomly:
- Network failure
- Tacho A failure
- SCSU controller overload
alarms.effect:
During dual fuel operation:
- Dual fuel shutdown
- Engine operation on fuel oil

During fuel oil operation:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable
alarms.suggested_action:
If SCSU continues to report this alarm, check: 
- CCU
- Network cabling

If SCSU randomly reports this failure, check:
- Network status. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Network Status'
- Network cabling and terminating resistors.
- For earth fault

alarms.long_description: SCSU did not receive a telegram network message from CCU.\n\nTelegram is sent from CCU once per revolution, after receiving fuel telegram, and contains information about engine speed, fuel indexes and injection timing etc.
alarms.cause:
If SCSU reports this alarm continuously:
- CCU failure

If SCSU reports this alarm randomly:
- Network failure
- Tacho A failure
- SCSU controller overload
alarms.effect:
During dual fuel operation:
- Dual fuel shutdown
- Engine operation on fuel oil

During fuel oil operation:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable
alarms.suggested_action:
If SCSU continues to report this alarm, check: 
- CCU
- Network cabling

If SCSU randomly reports this failure, check:
- Network status. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Network Status'
- Network cabling and terminating resistors.
- For earth fault
