alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Out. Pipe HC Concentration Shutdown
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Out. Pipe HC Concentration Shutdown
alarms.cause: - Second fuel leakage to outer pipe
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel shutdown\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action: - Pressurise sec fuel pipes. Go to: 'Second Fuel System' -> 'SF Pipes' and perform manual\nassembly test\n- Locate second fuel leakage according to manual

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: SF Temperature Stop - SF Stop
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: SF Temperature Stop - SF Stop
alarms.long_description: Second fuel temperature outside allowed range
alarms.cause: - Second fuel temperature deviates from setpoint, or\n- Sensor failure
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel Stop\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Alarm for temperature low / high
- Second fuel supply temperature
- Second fuel temperature sensor

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Seal Oil Pump Ctrl Failure - SF Stop
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Seal Oil Pump Ctrl Failure - SF Stop
alarms.long_description: Seal Oil Pump Ctrl Failure - SF Stop
alarms.cause:
- Seal oil pump starter panel  is off or manually set to 'Local', or
- Seal oil pump starter panel  failure, or
- Seal oil pump starter panel feedback failure, or
- Cable failure
alarms.effect:
During dual fuel operation:
- Dual fuel stop
- Engine operation on fuel oil

During fuel oil operation:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Starter panel control switch is set to 'Remote'
- Starter panel, main breaker and overcurrent pretection relay
- Cabling
- Seal oil pump. Go to: 'Second Fuel System' -> 'Seal Oil'

If all is OK: 'Set switch to 'Off' and wait a few seconds.
Reset switch to 'Remote'

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Manual Seal Oil Operation Demanded
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Manual Seal Oil Operation Demanded
alarms.long_description: Manual seal oil operation is enabled
alarms.cause: Seal oil operation was set to 'Manual' on MOP
alarms.effect:
- Dual Fuel operation unavailable
- Seal oil pump may be started manually from MOP

Caution:
Seal oil system should not be pressurised for long periods when not running on second fuel
alarms.suggested_action: Switch back to automatic operation after finishing manual operation

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Seal Oil Failure - SF Stop
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Seal Oil Failure - SF Stop
alarms.long_description: Seal Oil BuildUp Failure - SF Stop
alarms.cause: - Seal oil pump failure, or \n- Seal oil leakage
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel Stop\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- For seal oil leakages\n- Failing seal oil pump

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Seal Oil Pressure Failure - SF Stop
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Seal Oil Pressure Failure - SF Stop
alarms.long_description: Seal Oil Pressure Failure - SF Stop
alarms.cause:
- Seal oil system failure, or
- Seal oil filter clogged, or
- Seal oil system leakage, or
- Seal oil pressure sensor failure
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel Stop\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Seal oil system

Further troubleshooting. Go to: 'Second fuel' -> 'Seal Oil':
1. Start seal oil pump
2. Check seal oil pressure sensors

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: NMEA not receiving updates
alarms.long_description: NMEA not receiving updates, so time messages from the external clock are missing.
alarms.cause: Something is wrong among external Control System, cabling and MOP.
alarms.effect: ECS is unable to synchronize to the ship's clock.
alarms.suggested_action: Switch to internal clock in screen Admin - Set time\n2. Check communication cable.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->IO Configuration->Tacho->Missing TIU-A and TIU-B telegram
alarms.long_description: Missing network telegram message from both TIUA and TIUB
alarms.cause: TIUA and TIUB are not transmitting or\nThe TIUA/TIUB or CCU1 Controller network connection may be broken.\nCould also be a network switch failure
alarms.effect: TheCCU1 Controller due to no reception of engine information (speed, position and direction)
alarms.suggested_action:
If the alarm continues to stay active while engine runs, check: 
- Both TIU Controllers are powered on and LEDs indicates correct status
- Check switch LED status
- Network cabling between the TIU Controllers and switch
- Network cabling between the CCU1 Controller and switch

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->IO Configuration->Tacho->Missing TIU-A telegram
alarms.long_description: Missing network telegram message from TIUA
alarms.cause: TIUA and TIUB are not transmitting or\nThe TIUA/TIUB or CCU1 Controller network connection may be broken.\nCould also be a network switch failure
alarms.effect:
No redundant reception of engine information (speed, position and direction).
If both TIU telegrams are missing on same CCU1 Controller:
- No fuel injection on that unit
- No cylinder lubrication
- No exhaust valve movement
alarms.suggested_action:
If the alarm continues to stay active while engine runs, check: 
- Both TIU Controllers are powered on and LEDs indicates correct status
- Check switch LED status
- Network cabling between the TIU Controllers and switch
- Network cabling between the CCU1 Controller and switch

alarms.long_description: Missing network telegram message from TIUB
alarms.cause: TIUB is not transmitting or The TIUA or CCU1 Controller network connection may be broken. Could also be switch failure
alarms.effect:
No redundant reception of engine information (speed, position and direction).
If both TIU telegrams are missing on same CCU1 Controller:
- No fuel injection on that unit
- No cylinder lubrication
- No exhaust valve movement
alarms.suggested_action:
If the alarm continues to stay active while engine runs, check: 
- Both TIU Controllers are powered on and LEDs indicates correct status
- Check switch LED status
- Network cabling between the TIU Controllers and switch
- Network cabling between the CCU1 Controller and switch

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->IO Configuration->Tacho->Tacho Sys. ATC setup rejected
alarms.cause: Internal timing margin too small
alarms.effect: One Injection or exhaust valve closure might have been skipped. The controller will continue normal operation.
alarms.suggested_action: Please contact MAN-ES

alarms.synopsis: No Telegram Received from ECU A
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->IO Configuration->Fuel Telegram Handler->No Telegram Received from ECU A
alarms.long_description: CCU did not receive a fuel telegram network message from the ECU.\n\nFuel telegrams are sent once per revolution. Fuel telegrams contain injection and exhaust valve operation commands.
alarms.cause:
If all CCU reports this alarm continuously:
- ECU failure
If CCU reports this alarm randomly:
- Network failure
alarms.effect: - Redundancy reduced.\n- The CCU will continue normal operation, based on telegrams from redundant ECU.
alarms.suggested_action:
If different CCUs randomly report this failure, check:
- Network status on MOP maintenance screen.
- Network cabling, include terminating resistors.
- For ground failure.

If all CCUs permanently report this failure, check: 
- ECU 
- Network cabling

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->IO Configuration->Burst IO Handler->Too Late PSP Setup
alarms.long_description: Internal ECS failure. An internal calculation was completed too late.
alarms.cause: A partly failing network may cause significantly increased cpu load on the controllers, causing calculation delays.
alarms.effect: Often no effect. \nIn other situations unstable fuel injection and lubrication of one or more cylinders.
alarms.suggested_action:
Parameter adjustment may be required.

Until parameter adjustment is carried out, monitor exhaust gas temperature carefully:
- If temperature is OK: Continuous running is OK.
- If temperature NOT OK: Shut off affected cylinder. Reduce load and speed.

alarms.synopsis: SF Valve Ok Signal Forced True
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->IO Configuration->SecFuel Ok Signal For ECU->SF Valve Ok Signal Forced True
alarms.cause: - Parameter "SecFuel Ok Signal For ECU, Disable function,Force Outvar true" is set to Yes
alarms.effect:
SF Valve failure does no longer block SF operation.

GI Engines: 
ELGI position feedback supervision error does not block SF operation.
alarms.suggested_action: This alarm may only occur during special tests on test bed.\n\nIf this alarm occurs in service, please contact MAN-ES

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->IO Configuration->Gas Channel Relief Valve->Gas Channel Relief Pos. Fail
alarms.long_description: SF cylinder block: Gas Channel Relief Valve does not open during assembly test
alarms.cause:
SF cylinder block: 
 - Gas Channel Relief Valve does not open
 - Gas Channel Relief Valve position sensor is failing
 - Hydraulic leakage might prevent control of Gas Channel Relief Valve
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel Stop\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action:
SF cylinder block: 
 - Check position sensor for Gas Channel Relief Valve
 - Check cabling for Gas Channel Relief Valve
 - Check for hydraulic leakage

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->IO Configuration->Seal Oil Block Valve->Alarm Seal Oil Dev

alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->IO Configuration->DI,8114,Piston Cooling OutletSw->Warning: Physical input override
alarms.long_description: Manual I/O channel overriding active (on this channel).
alarms.cause: Manual I/O channel overriding for testing an input channel is active.
alarms.effect:
Manual I/O channel overriding an input or output channel is only for testing purposes.
Overriding:
 - Can cause hazardous situation and engine damage if used incorrectly!
 - Can cause or prevent alarms.
 - Can cause or prevent engine shut down/slow down.
 - Can cause or prevent duel SF stop or SF shut down.
alarms.suggested_action: Disable I/O channel override immediately after testing.\nLocate the overridden channel in the Maintenance -> system I/O view page. Manual channel override is indicated with a "!" in a yellow triangle in the Status column.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Command Handler->HCU Oil Leakage [SLD]
alarms.long_description: Leakage has been detected at the specified HCU
alarms.cause: A leakage is detected in the high pressure fuel pipe.
alarms.effect:
High pressure fuel is present in the outer pipe. 
A leakage in the outer pipe will result in fuel spray onto engine
components and maybe even on personnel. 
The control system provides an option (set by MAN-ES)
for stopping fuel injections on the specific cylinder during this situation.
alarms.suggested_action:
If automatic fuel cut out is not performed by ECS,
manually cut of fuel to that specific cylinder via the chief limiter on MOP.
Reduce engine load to acceptable level with 1 cylinder cut out.
Stop engine when possible and repair high pressure pipe.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Command Handler->HCU Oil Leakage/Relief Disc [SLD]
alarms.long_description: Leakage has been detected at the specified HCU or Relief Disk breakage has been detected at the specified CCU
alarms.cause: A leakage is detected in the high pressure fuel pipe, OR A high pressure in the cylinder have coursed a breakage of the Relief Disk in the relief valve system.
alarms.effect: High pressure fuel is in the outer pipe. A leakage in the outer pipe will result in fuel spray onto engine\ncomponents and maybe even on personnel.  OR Exhaust gas will pass through the Relief Disc hole. \nThe control system provides an option (set by MAN-ES) for stopping fuel injections on the specific cylinder during this situation.
alarms.suggested_action:
If automatic fuel cut out is not performed by ECS,
manually cut of fuel to that specific cylinder via the chief limiter on MOP.
Reduce engine load to acceptable level with 1 cylinder cut out.
Stop engine when possible and repair high pressure pipe.

alarms.long_description: Exhaust valve stopped due to HCU Leakage or Relief Disk alarm
alarms.cause: A leakage is detected in the high pressure fuel pipe, OR A high pressure in the cylinder have coursed a breakage of the Relief Disk in the relief valve system.
alarms.effect: Fuel injection stopped and no exhaust valve operation on affected cylinder.\n- Compression pressure limiter is activated.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Please refer to 6645-0320 Running with Cylinders or Turbochargers out of Operation
- Check relief Disk
- Check for HCU Leakage
- Check cabling

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Cylinder->Fuel Injection->FO Analog Injection->Inject Valve Reduced Lift Ctrl->PIV Control Oil Pressure Low
alarms.long_description: PIV activation pressure too low for Reduced Lift
alarms.cause:
- Hydralic oil leak, or\- PIV valve failure, or
- PIV cabling failure, or
- Pressure sensor failure, or
- Signal failure, or
- CCU1 Controller input channel failure
alarms.effect: Increased fuel oil consumption
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Hydraulic system for leaks 
- PIV valve
- Pressure sensor cabling

To reable reduced lift after checks have been made:
- Stop and start duel fuel

- Pressure sensor failure, or
- Signal failure, or
- CCU1 Controller input channel failure
alarms.effect: Reduced fuel oil injection on affected cylinder
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- PIV valve\n- Pressure sensor cabling

alarms.synopsis: FO: Burst and Prep sync missed
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Cylinder->Fuel Injection->FO Injection Validation->FO: Burst and Prep sync missed
alarms.long_description: Misfiring coursed by to early Injection Request
alarms.cause: Overload of the CPU, or to early injection request. This could be coursed by wrong parameter setting.
alarms.effect: One fuel injection was missing.
alarms.suggested_action: Check if the parameters has been changed recently.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Cylinder->Fuel Injection->FO Injection Validation->FO: Fuel Plunger Not Returned
alarms.long_description: Fuel plunger did not return to expected position before next injection.
alarms.cause:
- Fuel oil inlet pressure low, or
- Fuel pump suction valve failure, or 
- FIVA valve spool stuck, or 
- Fuel plunger stuck
alarms.effect: Injected fuel amount reduced. \nExhaust gas temperature decreased.\nReduced cylinder performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Fuel supply pressure
- Fuel oil suction valve

Further troubleshooting: 
1. Stop the engine at first opportunity. 
2. Go to 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU'
3. Activate 'Fuel Plunger' and 'Exhaust Valve' to test failing unit 
   
If FIVA movements and exhaust valve are OK: Perform one manual fuel injection attempt.

If manual attempt does not provide any fuel injection: Replace FIVA valve.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Cylinder->Fuel Injection->FO Injection Validation->FO: Fuel Plunger Stroke Too High

alarms.cause:
- Fuel pump suction valve failure, or 
- Injection valve failure, or
- Fuel supply pressure too low, or
- FIVA valve failure, or
- CCU failure
alarms.effect: Injected fuel amount incorrect. \nExhaust gas temperature deviation.\nReduced cylinder performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Fuel supply pressure
- Fuel oil suction valve
- Fuel injector valves 

Further troubleshooting: 
1. Stop the engine at first opportunity. 
2. Go to 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU'
3. Activate 'Fuel Plunger' and 'Exhaust Valve' to test failing unit 

If FIVA movements and exhaust valve are OK: Perform one manual fuel injection attempt.

If manual attempt does not provide any fuel injection: Replace FIVA valve

alarms.synopsis: FO: Fuel Plunger Stroke Too Low
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Cylinder->Fuel Injection->FO Injection Validation->FO: Fuel Plunger Stroke Too Low
alarms.long_description: Fuel plunger strokes are shorter than ordered by the engine control system.
alarms.cause:
- Injection valve failure, or 
- Fuel oil viscosity too high, or
- Hydraulic oil pressure too low, or 
- FIVA valve failure, or
- Fuel plunger stuck
alarms.effect: Injected fuel amount incorrect. \nExhaust gas temperature deviation.\nReduced cylinder performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Fuel injection valves
- Fuel viscosity
- Hydraulic oil pressure
Further troubleshooting:
1. Stop the engine at first opportunity.
2. Go to 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU'
3. Activate Fuel Plunger and Exhaust Valve to test failing unit
If FIVA movements and exhaust valve are OK: Perform one manual fuel injection attempt.
If manual attempt does not provide any fuel injection: Replace FIVA valve
If the problem persists: Replace fuel pump plunger and barrel

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Cylinder->Fuel Injection->FO Injection Validation->FO: Illegal Fuel Plng. Move [SLD]
alarms.long_description: The fuel plunger has made an illegal movement. \nRisk of untimed fuel injection.
alarms.cause: - Plunger position sensor or cable failure, or\n- ELFI / FIVA valve failure, or\n- CCU failure
alarms.effect:
No fuel injection due to risk of untimed fuel injection.

For FIVA installations:
- No exhaust valve operation 
- Slowdown is requested
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- CCU1 Controller Fuel plunger position sensor status
- Fuel plunger position sensor and cabling.

If the sensor is replaced, go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Function Test' to recalibrate the sensor. 

Reactivate fuel injection. Go to 'Engine' ->'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' -> 'HCU Status and Reset' to reset failing unit. 
Do not reactivate fuel injection until the cylinder unit is considered to be OK.

Further troubleshooting: 
1. Stop the engine at first opportunity. 
2. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU'
3. Test failing unit's fuel plunger operation

If the problem persists, replace or exchange, one part at a time: 
- Fuel plunger position sensor 
- Fuel plunger sensor cabling  
- ELFI / FIVA valve
- CCU

NOTE
Alarm can be overridden by invalidating CCU1 Controller FO Pump Plunger Position and reactivating fuel injection on 'Maintenance' -> 'System View I/O Test'

alarms.long_description: FO: FIVA/ELFI strokes are less than ordered by the engine control system.

alarms.effect: Injected fuel amount incorrect. \nExhaust gas temperature deviation.\nReduced cylinder performance.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Cylinder->Exhaust Valve->Exhaust Valve Supervision->Air Spring Supervision->Air Spring Pressure Low
alarms.long_description: Exhaust valve air spring pressure too low
alarms.cause: - Air spring leakage\n- Air spring supply blocked or shut off\n- Faulty pressure sensor
alarms.effect: Activating the exhaust valve with too low air spring pressure will damage the exhaust valve.
alarms.suggested_action:
Stop Exhaust valve operation immediately on MOP, 'Engine'->'Chief Limiters' -> 'Exhaust Valve Operation' (or power off CCU)

Check:
- Low force Reduction Station spring Air
- Air spring
- Pressure sensor

alarms.synopsis: Exh. Valve Open Stroke Too High
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Cylinder->Exhaust Valve->Exhaust Valve Supervision->Max Stroke Supervision->Exh. Valve Open Stroke Too High
alarms.long_description: Exhaust Valve Open Stroke too high
alarms.cause: - Too low air spring supply pressure, or\n- Air spring leakage, or\n- Faulty exhaustvalve position sensor
alarms.effect: If air spring pressure is too low, continuous operation may result in severe mechanical damage to the exhaust valve air spring disc.
alarms.suggested_action:
If a loud knocking sound is heard from the exhaust valve:
Stop exhaust valve operation immediately on MOP, 'Engine'->'Chief Limiters' -> 'Exhaust Valve Operation' (or power off CCU)


Check: 
- Air spring supply pressure
- Air spring
- Exhaust valve position sensor

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Cylinder->Exhaust Valve->Exhaust Valve Supervision->Exh.V. Close Stroke Low [SLD]
alarms.long_description: The exhaust valve closing stroke is too low (Slowdown)
alarms.cause:
- Accumulator pressure too low, or 
- De-aerating orifice in exhaust valve top blocked, or  
- Non-return valves for exhaust valve actuator oil inlet damaged, or
- No air supply or leaking exhaust valve air spring, or
- Exhaust valve position sensor failure, or
- ELVA/FIVA/WIVA valve failure

Note:
This alarm also occurs as a consequence of these alarms: 
- Illegal Fuel Plunger Movement 
- Illegal ELFI/FIVA/WIVA Position
- ELFI/FIVA/WIVA Feedback Signal Failure
- Frozen IO Detected
alarms.effect: - Fuel injection stopped on affected cylinder.\n- Compression pressure limiter is activated.\n- Slowdown is requested.
alarms.suggested_action:
Please refer to 6645-0320 Running with Cylinders or Turbochargers out of operation.
Check:
- Exhaust valve position sensor.
- Accumulator pressure.
- De-aerating orifice in exhaust valve top.
- Non-return valves for exhaust valve actuator oil inlet.
- Air spring supply pressure and perform drop-down test of exhaust valve spindle.
- ELFI / FIVA / WIVA valve.

alarms.effect:
-Slow-down is requested.
If the parameter "Close Pos Changed Fuel Cut Out" is  active then: 

-Fuel injection stopped on affected cylinder

If the parameter "Close Pos Changed Fuel Cut Out" is  passive then: 

-Reduced compression pressure.
-Increased exhaust gas and valve temperature.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Exhaust valve position sensor
- Accumulator pressure
- De-aerating orifice in exhaust valve top
- Non-return valves for exhaust valve actuator oil inlet
- Air spring supply pressure and perform drop-down test of exhaust valve spindle.
- ELFI / FIVA / WIVA valve

If the parameter "Close Pos Changed Fuel Cut Out" is  active then: 
Reactivate fuel injection, go to 'Engine' -> 'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' -> 'HCU Status and Reset' to reset failing
unit.
Do not reactivate fuel injection until the cylinder unit is considered to be OK.
Reactivation only possibly for speed below 'HCU ReEnable Max Speed'

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Cylinder->Exhaust Valve->MEV Timing Controller->Return delay out of range
alarms.long_description: Measured ME-V return delay out of range. ME-V piston movement is too fast or too slow.
alarms.cause:
- Failing ELFI/FIVA Valve
- Failing piston feedback sensor,
- Too high friction in ME-V timing unit (too slow),
- Leakages in timing unit (too fast)
alarms.effect: ECS not able to control exhaust valve timing. Deviation on cylinder compression pressure may be present. Risk of too high compression and maximum pressure.
alarms.suggested_action:
Reduce Engine load to reduce compression and maximum pressure.

Adjust actual compression and maximum pressure on MOP.

Check:
- ELFI/FIVA alarms
- ME-V Piston feedback sensor
- For leakages at timing unit.

Use 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> HCU Events on MOP-B to compare ME-V piston feedback signal to other units.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Cylinder->FO ElFi Valve->FO ELFI Fdbck Fail.[SLD]

- Internal ELFI feedback failure

This alarm also occurs as a consequence of these alarms: 
- Illegal ELFI/FIVA Position
- Frozen IO Detected
alarms.effect: No fuel injection.\nSlowdown is requested.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check ELFI feedback cabling.

Go to 'Engine' -> 'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' -> 'HCU Status and Reset' to reset failing unit 

Further troubleshooting:
1. Stop the engine at first opportunity 
2. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU' 
3. Test failing unit's injection and exhaust valve operation. 
4. Compare signals from failing unit to signals from a well functioning unit. 

If the problem persists replace or exchange, one part at a time: 
- ELFI valve
- ELFI cabling
- CCU

alarms.effect: - Increased wear of cylinder liners\n- Risk of breakage of piston rings\n- Too high load on crosshead bearings
alarms.suggested_action:
Immediate Action:
Reduce "Pmax Offset" on actual cylinder unit to lower Pmax below alarm limit.
Troubleshooting:
1.Check that current Pcomp "Deviation" for the actual cylinder unit is within tolerances.
If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing "Pcomp/Pscav Offset" on the actual cylinder unit
manually or via Auto Tuning (Pcomp Deviation ->Pcomp).
2.Check that current Pmax "Deviation" for the actual cylinder unit is within tolerances.
If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing "Pmax Offset" for the actual cylinder unit
manually or via Auto Tuning (Pmax Deviation ->Pmax).
If unable to achieve correct Pcomp (in step 2) then please do not use Auto Tuning functionality and
keep "Pmax Offset" reduced manually on actual cylinder unit below alarm limit.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Module unavail.
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

- Network cabling between the TIU Controllers and switch
- Network cabling between the ECUA Controller and switch

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->Cylinder Lubrication->ACOM Lube->BN Value Feedback Failure
alarms.long_description: BN Value Feedback channel has signal error
alarms.cause: - ACOM Unit Failure: (ACOM System reports internal failure by a 2 mA signal to ECS) \n- Cabling or Signal Failure
alarms.effect: - ACOM System may not be working or is not working correctly\n- ACOM Mix may  not match what is ordered from ECS\n- Ordered BN Value is set to High BN
alarms.suggested_action: - Check Cabling\n- Check ACOM System

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->Cylinder Lubrication->Cylinder lubrication insufficient
alarms.long_description: Requested cylinder lubrication oil injection is greater than one full stroke per revolution on one or more units.
alarms.cause:
The Cylinder Lubrication Oil Feed Rate needed is too high. 

- High operator defined feed rate demand (g/kWh). Cylinder feed rate adjusted to a high value at high engine load, or 
- High sulfur neutralization demand, due to abnormally high sulfur content in Fuel Oil or Fuel Mix, and/or 
- Cylinder lubrication oil used has a too low BN number to support sufficient neutralization.
alarms.effect: The cylinder lubricator will be activated with the highest frequency possible, one per revolution.  \n\nUnder the current conditions the engine cannot maintain requested feed rate, risking excessive wear to the cylinders.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check cylinder lubrication screen and verify that the cylinder lubrication oil settings are in accordance with recommendations. 

Decrease engine load to reduce the amount of cylinder oil needed. 

If the issue is caused by a high sulfur neutralization demand, change cylinder oil to have a higher BN number. 

If problem persist contact MAN Energy Solutions.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->AutoTuning->Tuning Calculation->ContinuousTuning PI (online FQA)->Online FQA exceeds limits

alarms.suggested_action:

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->AutoTuning->Tuning Calculation->Sensor Supervision->Cylinder pressure deviation
alarms.long_description: Cylinder pressure measurement deviates more from average value than alarm limit.
alarms.cause:
Could be caused by malfunctioning of:

- Fuel valves

- Exhaust valve actuator
- FIVA valve

ECS alarms for too high Pmax, too high Prise and alarm for Cylinder pressure deviation are no longer
available.
Engine balancing and load distribution might be effected.
alarms.suggested_action: Carry out troubleshooting on above mentioned equipment.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->AutoTuning->Tuning Calculation->Prise Supervision->Average Prise above allowed value
alarms.long_description: Average Prise has exceeded Pmax-Pcomp alarm limit.
alarms.cause: Too low Compression Pressure or too high Maximum Pressure
alarms.effect: - Increased wear of cylinder liners\n- Risk of breakage of piston rings\n- Too high load on crosshead bearings
alarms.suggested_action:
Immediate Action:
Reduce "Pmax Offset All" to lower average Prise below alarm limit.
Troubleshooting:
1.Check that "Estimated Engine Load" (as shown on MOP) is correct by comparing with PMI
equipment and/or torquemeter.
If incorrect then utilize Fuel Quality feature for adjusting estimated engine load.
2.Check that average "Current Pcomp" and "Ordered Pcomp" are equal (within tolerances).
If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing "Pcomp/Pscav Offset All" manually or via Auto
Tuning (Pcomp mean value).
3.Check that average "Current Pmax" and "Ordered Pmax" are equal (within tolerances).
If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing Pmax Offset All manually or via Auto Tuning
(Pmax mean value).
If unable to achieve correct Pcomp (in step 2) then Pscav might be too low. This could be due to
severe ambient conditions or malfunctioning of exhaust gas bypass etc. Please do not use Auto
Tuning functionality and keep "Pmax Offset All" reduced manually below alarm limit.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->AutoTuning->Tuning Calculation->Prise Supervision->Cyl 1. Prise above allowed value
alarms.long_description: Prise has exceeded Pmax-Pcomp alarm limit.
alarms.cause: Too low Compression Pressure or too high Maximum Pressure
alarms.effect: - Increased wear of cylinder liners\n- Risk of breakage of piston rings\n- Too high load on crosshead bearings
alarms.suggested_action:
Immediate Action:
Reduce "Pmax Offset" on actual cylinder unit to lower Prise below alarm limit.
Troubleshooting:

manually or via Auto Tuning (Pcomp Deviation ->Pcomp).

manually or via Auto Tuning (Pmax Deviation ->Pmax).
If unable to achieve correct Pcomp (in step 2) then please do not use Auto Tuning functionality and
keep "Pmax Offset" reduced manually on actual cylinder unit below alarm limit.

alarms.cause:
- Fuel quality has changed more than allowed by the automatic adjustment.

alarms.effect: - The engine load estimation is not fully correct, which may cause fuel index limiters to be incorrect.\n- Prise and Pcomp/Pscav set points might deviate from design values.\n- Cylinder oil feed rate might be incorrect.

Check:
- That fuel quality is as expected.

- Check Fuel Pumps.
- WIF content is correct.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->Load Reduction Supervision Group->Pmax Supervision->Average Pmax above allowed value
alarms.long_description: Average Pmax has exceeded alarm limit
alarms.cause: Too high Maximum Pressure
alarms.effect:
- Increased wear of cylinder liners
- Risk of breakage of piston rings
- Too high load on crosshead bearings
- The limiter "Compression pressure" may be activated
alarms.suggested_action:
Immediate Action:
Reduce "Pmax Offset All" to lower average Pmax below alarm limit.
Troubleshooting:
1.Check that "Estimated Engine Load" (as shown on MOP) is correct by comparing with PMI
equipment and/or torquemeter.
If incorrect then utilize Fuel Quality feature for adjusting estimated engine load.
2.Check that average "Current Pcomp" and "Ordered Pcomp" are equal (within tolerances).
If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing "Pcomp/Pscav Offset All" manually or via Auto
Tuning (Pcomp mean value).
3.Check that average "Current Pmax" and "Ordered Pmax" are equal (within tolerances).
If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing "Pmax Offset All" manually or via Auto Tuning
(Pmax mean value).
If unable to achieve correct Pcomp (in step 2) then Pscav might be too high. This could be due to
severe ambient conditions or malfunctioning of exhaust gas bypass etc. Please do not use Auto
Tuning functionality and keep "Pmax Offset All" reduced manually below alarm limit.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->Load Reduction Supervision Group->Load Reduction State Machine->Compression Pres. Lim Active
alarms.cause: An alarm and scavenging air pressure above the safe limit has caused the "Compression Pressure Limiter" to activate

alarms.suggested_action: - Follow the suggested actions for the alarm(s) that caused the "Compression Pressure Limiter"  to activate\n- If the alarm(s) causing the activation of the "Compression Pressure Limiter" are disappeared, the limiter may be reset on the "Chief Limiters" MOP screen.\n- The "Compression Pressure Limiter" may be cancelled on the "Chief Limiters" MOP screen, but this can result in high compression pressure and unsafe operation.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->Load Reduction Supervision Group->Load Reduction State Machine->Compression Pres. Lim Cancelled
alarms.long_description: The "Compression Pressure Limiter" is disabled manually
alarms.cause: The "Compression Pressure Limiter" is cancelled manually on the MOP
alarms.effect: - The "Compression Pressure Limiter" is no longer active.\n- No safeguard against high compression pressure.\n- Too high compression pressure may cause cylinder cover lift.
alarms.suggested_action: - Reduce engine load as soon as possible\n- Reactivate the "Compression Pressure Limiter" at the "Chief Limiters" MOP screen as soon as possible to ensure safe operation.

- Decrease Pmax for the unit in question.

- Perform drain oil analysis, all units.
- Perform piston ring inspection at first opportunity.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->Exhaust Temp. Monitoring->CCU1-Exh. Temp. Dev Alm
alarms.long_description: Cylinder Exhaust gas temperature TT 8702 is higher than allowed deviation limit.
alarms.cause:
-Engine is not ballanced.
- Wear of Fuel injection valve. 
- Wear or malfunctioning FIVA valve.
- Malfunctioning fuel oil suction valve or pump.
- Pistion ring blow-by.
-Exhaust gas valve spindle and seat for leakage.
- Exhaust gas temperature sensor drifting.
alarms.effect:
-Dual Fuel Stop. 
- Reduced engine performance.
-Risk of increased wear on cylinder liner, piston and piston rings.
- Risk of fuel injector nozzle damage. 
-Risk of exhaust valve spindle or seat burning.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check: 
- Cylinder pressure balance, ACCo or Autotuning.
-Fuel injection valve: Opening pressure, atomization and visual inspection of spindle and seat.
-Fuel oil pump and suction valve for wear.
- Temperature sensor:Local thermometer also shows high exhaust gas temperature on the exhaust gas valve outlet and Electric connection to the temperature sensor.
-Piston ring blow-by.
-Exhaust gas valve spindle and seat for leakage.
-If mean indicated pressure PI is high check FIVA proportional valve: i.e. by comparing HCU event with other units or exchange the proportional valve with the one on another cylinder.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->Exhaust Temp. Monitoring->CCU1 Exh. Temp. High Alm
alarms.long_description: Cylinder Exhaust gas temperature TT 8702 above Normal service high
alarms.cause: -Wear or fouling of turbocharger. \n-Scavenging air cooler:calcium block up in water side or fouling in the air side.\n- Fouling in the exhaust gas boiler (high DeltaP over Exhaust Gas boiler).
alarms.effect:
-Dual Fuel Stop. 
- Reduced engine performance.
-Risk of increased wear on cylinder liner, piston and piston rings.
- Risk of fuel injector nozzle damage. 
-Risk of exhaust valve spindle or seat burning.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
-Turbocharger for wear and fouling:Exhaust gas side (TC rotor wear / Nozzle ring fouling) and Air side for fouling (Air filter / compressor).
-Scavenging air cooler:Water side for calcium block up (drain tank) and Air side for fouling.
-Check the Exhaust gas boiler for fouling.
-Very high ambient air temperature at compressor inlet can lead to high exhaust gas temperature at high load.

alarms.cause:
-Engine is not ballanced.
- Wear of Fuel injection valve.

- Malfunctioning fuel oil suction valve or pump.
- Pistion ring blow-by.
-Exhaust gas valve spindle and seat for leakage.

alarms.effect:

- Reduced engine performance.
-Risk of increased wear on cylinder liner, piston and piston rings.
- Risk of fuel injector nozzle damage. 
-Risk of exhaust valve spindle or seat burning.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->Active EngRunMode Not Calibrated
alarms.long_description: Fuel index for Active Engine Running Mode is currently not calibrated.
alarms.cause:
The calibration of the fuel index for Active Engine Running Mode has not been completed. 
While the engine is on the test bed and the calibration of the Engine Running Mode is not 
completed this Alarm will occur. The calibration of engine running mode must be completed, 
and alarm must be cleared, before delivery test
alarms.effect: The Load calculation has reduced accuracy in this mode, which may result in engine overload or insufficient power delivery.
alarms.suggested_action: The Alarm will go away upon completion of the calibration of the Active Engine Running Mode.\nThis alarm should only occur while the engine is on test bed and during commission. \nIf this alarm occurs while the engine is in service contact the engine builder.

alarms.effect: Manual pressure control is active. \nEngine cannot be started from bridge.\nManual set point will be overruled, when HPS returns to automatic operation.
alarms.suggested_action: Switch back to automatic control as soon as manual operation is completed

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Driven Pumps Command->Changing press. ctrl. pump
alarms.cause:
- No position feedback signal from proportional valve, or 
- No swash plate position feedback signal, or 
- Proportional valve amplifier failure, or 
- Mechanical pump failure
alarms.effect:
ECS will attempt to deliver full flow:
- Full flow ahead, if engine runs ahead
- Full flow astern, if engine runs astern

If two or more pumps fail:
Engine may not be able to run astern.

In case of mechanical pump failure: ECS may deliver low or no flow to the HPS.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check cabling to and from: 
- Proportional valve
- Proportional valve amplifier
- LVDT amplifier 
- ECUA Controller 
    
Check pump and proportional valve

Go to 'Auxiliaries' -> 'Hydraulic System' -> 'Failed pump' to reset failure state.

Further troubleshooting:
1. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HPS'
2. Test failing pump swashplate operation.
3. Compare signals from failing pump to signals from a well functioning pump.

- Hydraulic leakage

alarms.long_description: Electric motor cannot be controlled by the engine control system
alarms.cause:
- Electric motor switchboard is off or manually set to 'Local', or
- Electric motor switch board failure, or
- Switchboard feedback failure, or
- Cabling failure
alarms.effect: If the failure is in the feedback part only: No effect\nElse: No ECS control of electric motor
alarms.suggested_action: Check the startup pump operation control switch at the startup pump switchboard. The ECS expect the switch to be in the "Remote" control position. alarms.effect: Electrical driven Backup pump is started. Abnormal pump control states might damage the hydraulic pumps. The Electrical pump will continue to run and might not be able to sustain hydraulic pressure once engine is stopped.
alarms.suggested_action: Check hydraulic system.

alarms.suggested_action:

If the problem persists, check:

- RCS signals

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Self Controlling HPS Cmd->Pump Start/Stop Control->Slave Start/Stop State Machine->Master/Slave Pump Not Running
alarms.long_description: The Engine Control System (ECS) expects more pumps to run but only zero or one "Running" signal is currently present.
alarms.cause: - Could be caused by wrong running signal or failed pump(s).\n- Could be wrong switch settings on the HPS starter cabinet.
alarms.effect: - No effect if both HPS pumps are running.\n- If only one pump is running the maximum obtainable load will be limited depending on engine configuration. Normally minimum 55% engine load should be possible.\n- If no pumps are running the engine will stop.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check  Pump start signal:
1) Pump 1 connected to ACU1 Controller Start Up Pump start/stop
2) Pump 2 connected to ACU2 Conttroller Start Up Pump start/stop

- Check cabling to Pump 1 and Pump 2 running signals.
(ACU1 Start Up Pump running)
(ACU2 Start Up Pump running).

alarms.synopsis: Slave Pump Started Due to Error(s)
alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Self Controlling HPS Cmd->Pump Start/Stop Control->Slave Start/Stop State Machine->Slave Pump Started Due to Error(s)
alarms.long_description: Normally the ECS only starts the Slave pump when the engine load is above a certain limit. In case of certain errors the Slave pump is ordered started
alarms.cause: - Hydraulic Pressure is not valid\n- Setpoint too high compared to actual pressure (Alarm for "Hydr. Press. Regulator High Fail" could also be present!)\n- Missing Pump (Master/Slave pump switched off or missing valid running signals.)
alarms.effect: - No effect if both HPS pumps are running.\n- If only one pump is running the maximum obtainable load will be limited depending on engine configuration. Normally minimum 55% engine load should be possible.\n- If no pumps are running the engine will stop.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check  Pump start signal:
1) Pump 1 connected to ACU1 Controller Start Up Pump start/stop
2) Pump 2 connected to ACU2 Conttroller Start Up Pump start/stop

- Depending on the type of error that caused this alarm to be raised check the following:
a) Cabling to Hydraulic pressure sensor.
b) Network or tacho alarms on MOP.
c) Hydraulic Pressure Setpoint deviation too large compared to measured pressure.
d) Missing pump running signals.

- Check cabling to Pump 1 and Pump 2 running signals.
(ACU1 Start Up Pump running)
(ACU2 Start Up Pump running).

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Self Controlling HPS Cmd->Pump Start/Stop Control->Missing Pump (Deviation)

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Self Controlling HPS Cmd->Pump Start/Stop Control->Pump 1 not running
alarms.long_description: The hydraulic pump should run because the engine is running.
alarms.cause: The pump does not give a "Running" signal.
alarms.effect: - Maximum engine load is limited if pump is not running.\n- The Engine Control System (ECS) have ordered the HPS slave pump to start. The slave pump will be running until both Pump running signals have been detected On.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check if the pump is running.\n- if it is running check the cable giving a "Running" signal to ECS.\n- In case the Pump running signal turns On/Off and triggers the slave pump to start/stop go to the HPS starter cabinets and move switch to "Pump 1 & 2". This will disable control of the slave pump by the ECS. Move the switch to "Pump 1 Master" or "Pump 2 Master" after the problem has been solved.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Self Controlling HPS Cmd->Pump Start/Stop Control->Pump 2 not running
alarms.long_description: The hydraulic pump should run because the engine is running.
alarms.cause: The pump does not give a "Running" signal.
alarms.effect: - Maximum engine load is limited if pump is not running.\n- The Engine Control System (ECS) have ordered the HPS slave pump to start. The slave pump will be running until both Pump running signals have been detected On.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check if the pump is running.\n- if it is running check the cable giving a "Running" signal to ECS.\n- In case the Pump running signal turns On/Off and triggers the slave pump to start/stop go to the HPS starter cabinets and move switch to "Pump 1 & 2". This will disable control of the slave pump by the ECS. Move the switch to "Pump 1 Master" or "Pump 2 Master" after the problem has been solved.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Self Controlling HPS Cmd->Set Point Adaption->Hydraulic Press. Adaptation [bar]
alarms.cause: This can be caused by ECUs having been offline, and is now reconnected.
alarms.effect: This should not have any effect. The value should be overwritten by the controlling ECU and the alarm should no longer be present.
alarms.suggested_action:
No action should be needed.

If the alarm occurs often allowed deviation may be too low - Contact
MAN-ES

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Self Controlling HPS Cmd->Set Point Adaption->Hydr. Press. Regulator High Fail
alarms.long_description: The automatic pressure control could not achieve correct pressure. Hydraulic pressure lower than desired.
alarms.cause: - HPS pumps do not deliver as high pressure as expected, or\n- leakage has increased, or\n- electrical connection to HPS is failing.
alarms.effect: Too low pressure may reduce injections and slow down the engine - in extreme cases stop the engine.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check cabling to HPS (e.g. using manual control).
Check pressure sensor.
Check for hydraulic leakages.
Check Swash Plate Indicators.
Check that there are no other alarms for Pumps missing.
Check switch settings on HPS starter cabinets are in normal position.

If all checks above are ok, the HPS proportional valve may need to be recalibrated.

NOTE:
The HPS switch setting on starter cabinet should be set to "Pump 1 Master" or "Pump 2 Master". If the switch is in "Pump 1 & 2" then both HPS pumps should run.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Self Controlling HPS Cmd->Set Point Adaption->Hydr. Press. Regulator Low Fail
alarms.long_description: The automatic pressure control could not achieve correct pressure. Hydraulic pressure higher than desired.
alarms.cause: - HPS pumps deliver higher pressure than expected, or\n- Leakage has decreased.
alarms.effect: Too high pressure can result in excessive electrical power consumption.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check cabling to HPS (e.g. using manual control).
Check pressure sensor.
Check for hydraulic leakages.
Check Swash Plate Indicators.
Check that there are no other alarms for Pumps missing.
Check switch settings on HPS starter cabinets are in normal position.

If all checks above are ok, the HPS proportional valve may need to be recalibrated.

NOTE:
The HPS switch setting on starter cabinet should be set to "Pump 1 Master" or "Pump 2 Master". If the switch is in "Pump 1 & 2" then both HPS pumps should run.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Self Controlling HPS Cmd->Mode Handler (Manual/Auto)->Manual Hydr. Press Control
alarms.cause: Manual Activated
alarms.effect:
The HPS will "bumpless" change to Manual operation. The pressure setpoint can be overruled by the operator by manually altering the pressure setpoint. The new pressure setpoint will be used until the operator either selects a new setpoint, or returns to Automatic mode.

NOTE:
A large increase in setpoint could trigger the HPS slave pump to start. Therefore it is recommended to limit the steps to about 20 bar.
alarms.suggested_action:
Switch to Automatic operation when manual operation is ended.

NOTE:
In case the ECS setpoint in automatic operation is more than 20 bar above the manual setpoint, increase the manual pressure setpoint, before switching out of manual operation.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Self Controlling HPS Cmd->Pressure Decay Measuring->Hydraulic Pressure fell too quickly
alarms.long_description: Hydraulic pressure fell too quickly after all pumps were stopped.
alarms.cause: Hydraulic leakage or failing accumulator(s).
alarms.effect: Hydraulic leakage or failing accumulators may cause problems when the engine is started again.\nCorrect these failures before attempting normal running.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for Hydraulic leakage and check accumulator pressure.\n- Investigate all HCU's by cutting off relevant valves. Do this one HCU at a time and evaluate leakage result.

alarms.effect:
Engine control system will use the other sensors to evaluate the hydraulic inlet pressure. 

NOTE
If the pump inlet valve is closed, engine start will cause pump cavitation
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Pump inlet valve\n- Pump inlet pressure sensor

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Hyd. press. sensor ACU 1 deviates
alarms.long_description: Hydraulic oil pressure sensor (1201-x) on this ACU deviates from the hydraulic oil pressure sensors on the two other ACUs.
alarms.cause:
a. Hydraulic pump failure, or
b. Sensor failure, or
c. ECUA Controller failure, or 
d. Cable failure
alarms.effect:
If a:
Engine performance may be reduced due to reduced hydraulic capacity.

If b, c, and d:
No effect on engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
a. Hydraulic pump
b. Cabling
c. ECUA Controller
d. Sensor

If a, hydraulic pump failure:
1. Reduce engine load until stable engine performance is achieved
2. Check other alarms
3. Check pump and pump drive shaft

If b, c, or d:
Repair or replace failing part

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Pump inlet press. low
alarms.long_description: Lubrication oil inlet  pressure is low.
alarms.cause: - Sensor failure, or\n- Lubrication oil supply pump(s) not running, or \n- Inlet valve closed
alarms.effect:
No effect.

NOTE
If system oil pressure drops below shutdown level: 
Engine control system will request shutdown.
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Inlet pressure sensors \n- Lubrication oil supply system(pumps, valves, etc)

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Hyd. press. deviates from setpoint
alarms.long_description: The hydraulic pressure deviates from the hydraulic pressure set point calculated by the engine control system
alarms.cause: - Hydraulic system leakage, or\n- Engine driven pump failure, or\n- Engine driven pump calibration failure
alarms.effect: If the hydraulic pressure is lower than the ECS computed setpoint and it continues to decrease, the hydraulic pumps cannot deliver enough oil to maintain the pressure. If the pressure drops below 145 - 150 bar, the ECS is likely to carry out a shutdown. If the pressure is too high, it could lead to increased injection pressure.
alarms.suggested_action:
Reduce engine load until stable engine performance is achieved.

Check:
- Hydraulic system for leaks
- Engine driven pump

If engine has only 2 engine driven pumps and the pressure is too high, then manually open relief valve pos 307 to reduce pressure to 225 bar equal to the setting of pressure reduction valve pos. 308.

If the problem persists: Recalibrate engine driven pump on MOP

alarms.synopsis: High CR Fuel Press During Circ.
alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->CR Supply Command->Command State Machine->High CR Fuel Press During Circ.
alarms.long_description: High CR Fuel Pressure during circulation
alarms.cause: - CR Pumps running signals missing\n- Defect CR Combivalves\n- Defect Cabling to CR Combivalves
alarms.effect: Circulation of fuel though CR pumps and CR injection valves is not possible. This may lead to fuel blocking in CR pumps and CR injection valves.
alarms.suggested_action: 1. Check CR pumps running signal\n2. Check cabling to CR Combivalves\n3. Check CR Combivalve

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->CR Supply Command->Command State Machine->CR Supply Command State (Deviation
alarms.long_description: ECUA and ECUB are generating differing output values for controller state
alarms.cause: Deviation between redundant input signals to ECU A and ECU B or redundant parameters on ECU A and ECU B
alarms.effect: Redundancy reduced\nNo immediate effect on engine operation.\nIf the reduced redundancy causes CR fuel pressure issues other alarms will be raised.
alarms.suggested_action:
If the problem persists:
- Reset ECUA Controller when engine is stopped
- Check ECU cabling
- Check ACU cabling
- Check RCS signals

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->CR Supply Command->Controlling Pump Selection->Sensor Evaluation->CR Pressure Deviation

alarms.suggested_action: Use CR MOP screen to identifying the deviating sensor\n- Check failing sensor

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->CR Supply Command->Combi Valve Supervision->Combi Valve A->CR Combivalve Illegal Open
alarms.long_description: Combi valve open position detected, when it should be closed
alarms.cause: - Combi valve "limp home" activated due to high CR pressure\n- CR pump control failure
alarms.effect: Time limited engine operation is possible as the combi valve will be worn out during "lime home, which eventually can cause loss of CR pressure and shutdown
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- CR pumps for control failure
- CR pumps set point and pressure feedback signal
- As soon as possible restart engine to reset the alarm

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU->IO->DI,2152-B,Local: Inc. Limiters->2152-B-Local: Inc. Limiters-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->IO->DO,2159-B,Inc. Limit Indication->2159-B-Inc. Limit Indication-Module unavail.
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU->IO->DR,2005-B,Reset Shut Down->2005-B-Reset Shut Down-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

- Sensor

If the problem persists: Replace the corresponding module on ECUB

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU->Propulsion Unit->Engine->Start/Stop Logic->Turning Failed
alarms.long_description: Engine slow turning attempt failed\nEngine was not turned sufficiently
alarms.cause: - Starting air system failure, or\n- ECUB is controlling
alarms.effect: Engine may not be able to start.\nSlow-turning valve is not wired to ECUB and Engine start that require slow-turning will fail.
alarms.suggested_action:
1. Check ECUA is controlling
2. Check slow turning valve
3. Turn engine by turning gear to a different position
4. Retry manual slow turn before new engine start

If the problem persists, check:
- Start air pressure
- Starting air pilot valves
- Starting valves

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->IO Terminals->AI,1618-1,EGR Blower 1 Speed FB->1618-1-EGR Blower 1 Speed FB-No Connection
alarms.cause:
- Cabling failure, or
- Sensor failure, or
- Supervision resistor across the switch is missing, or 
- EGRCU Controller input channel failure
alarms.effect: Reduced supervision. May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cabling
- Sensor
- Supervision resistor 
- EGRCU Controller input channel: 'Maintenance' -> 'System View I/O Test'

If the problem persists: Replace the corresponding module on EGRCU

alarms.long_description: AI or 'DI by Analog' Channel overload.

alarms.effect: Signal value is outside the safe range of the Channel and cannot be measured.\nMay reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action: Please check cabling and/or sensor..

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->IO Terminals->AI,1618-1,EGR Blower 1 Speed FB->1618-1-EGR Blower 1 Speed FB-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->IO Terminals->AI,1618-1,EGR Blower 1 Speed FB->1618-1-EGR Blower 1 Speed FB-Module unavail.
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

alarms.effect:
- EGR system is stopped.
- EGR system cannot start again while the alarm condition is present.

Check:
- Open switch and close switch.
- Air/electrical supply to the valve.
- Control valve.
- That the valve is not stuck.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->Supervision->EGR Gas Supervision->Temperature Supervision->Temperature WMC out Supervision->T-WMC out Too High->T-WMC out Too High
alarms.long_description: The temperature in the EGR Water Mist Catcher (WMC) outlet is too high.
alarms.cause: - Temperature sensor error.\n- Insufficient cooling of the EGR gas.\n- Deposits on cooler fins.
alarms.effect: - EGR system is stopped.\n- EGR system cannot start again while the alarm condition is present.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Temperature sensor and cable.
- Check if there is sufficient cooling water flow and check temperature on inlet and outlet of cooling water.
- If there is deposits on the cooler fins. 
- If there is corrosion in the cooling water pipes.
- If problem persists check for internal leakage (gas-water-mixing is by-passing the EGR-cooler).

alarms.synopsis: T WMC out Too High (TC cut-in)
alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->Supervision->EGR Gas Supervision->Temperature Supervision->T WMC out Too High (TC cut-in)
alarms.long_description: The temperature in the EGR Water Mist Catcher (WMC) outlet is too high.
alarms.cause: - Temperature sensor error.\n- Fouling on the air side.\n- Fouling on the water side.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Temperature sensor and cable.
- Check if there is sufficient cooling water flow and check temperature on inlet and outlet of cooling water.
- If there is fouling of the air side of the cooler, check the pressure drop over the EGR unit (PDT1689) and take necessary action.
- Check the water inlet/outlet temperature drop for deviations from normal values.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->Supervision->EGR Gas Supervision->O2 Sensor Supervision (OSU)->O2 Sensor1, not ready
alarms.long_description: O2 sensor is not ready for measuring.
alarms.cause:
If the engine is stopped and no auxiliary blowers are running, the O2 sensors will not be able to measure because they require a certain gas flow in order to work correctly.

Other causes:
- O2 sensor failures.
- Too low gas flow through the O2 sensor.
- Cable failure.
alarms.effect: No measuring is possible for this O2 sensor until it returns a ready signal.
alarms.suggested_action: - Reboot PLC in OSU Junction box.\n- Check cabling and proper termination for CANbus.\n- Replace sensor.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->Supervision->EGR Water Supervision->pH Supervision->Both pH Sensors Failing Suprv.->Both pH Sensors Failing
alarms.long_description: The signals from both pH sensors are out of range. Each sensor should give a signal between 4 mA to 20 mA.
alarms.cause:
- Failure in the cabling to the sensor.
- Sensor failure.
- Incorrect Sensor Calibration.
- Missing sensor power supply.
alarms.effect: - EGR system is stopped.\n- EGR system cannot start again while the alarm condition is present.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check the pH-sensor manual for trouble-shooting.
- Check for fuse alarms on MOP alarm screen. If no fuse alarms then:
- Check cabling to the sensor, according to the installation drawings.
- Check power supply to the sensor (measure voltage between A (negative) and D (positive)). If voltage is OK (18-32 Vdc): Replace sensor.
- Try to invalidate the signal on the EGRCU Controller. This could force the input signal to obtain a different value if this is needed.

- Short term: Invalidate the input from the faulty pH-sensor - or unplug the signal at the EGRCU Controller. When the signal is out of range or invalidated ECS will disregard the input and EGR-control can continue with only one pH-sensor.
-Long term: Stop EGR and dismount the faulty pH-sensor for calibration and trouble-shooting. Check the pH-sensor manual for further trouble-shooting.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->Supervision->EGR Water Supervision->WTS Supervision->WTS running deviation supervision->WTS running deviation
alarms.long_description: ECS does not receive matching running signal from EGR Water Treatment System (WTS) when run command is sent, within the defined time.
alarms.cause: - Malfunction in WTS.\n- Broken cable to WTS.
alarms.effect:
It is possible to continue EGR operation by accepting to run EGR without WTS before timeout (ECS MOP => Auxiliaries => EGR => EGR Water => Accept to Run EGR without Water Treatment System).

In case of EGR operation without WTS has been accepted:
- EGR system will continue running without WTS.
- EGR system can be started while the alarm is present.
- Increased risk of clogging the EGR pre-spray, EGR cooler and pump pre-filter (In case of clogging ECS will raise an alarm and stop EGR).
- Increasing water level in WTS buffer tank (In case of too high level ECS will raise an alarm and stop EGR).

In case of EGR operation without WTS has not been accepted before timeout:
- EGR system is stopped.
- EGR system cannot start while the alarm is present.
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- WTS operating panel. When the problem has been identified remember to acknowledge all alarms on the local WTS operating panel.\n- Cabling to WTS.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->Plant Control->System Control->Manually Run EGR Water Activated
alarms.long_description: Manually Run EGR Water is activated.

alarms.effect: EGR Water system will be run.
alarms.suggested_action: CAUTION: Only pump, valve or (WHS2: Buffer Tank level) failure will automatically stop EGR Water. The remaining EGR Water failures will only trigger alarms without stopping EGR Water. It is therefore extremely important to be aware of the possible alarms which may occur during EGR Water manual operation.\nWhen finishing EGR Water exercise and/or cleaning:\n- Deactivate Manually Run EGR Water on EGR Water screen.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRI1->System->Watchdogs deactivated
alarms.cause: This alarm should not happen in Service
alarms.effect: No effect on engine performance. The EGRI1 Controller may respond incorrectly to any software and hardware failures.
alarms.suggested_action: If this alarm occurs while the engine is in service please contact MAN-ES

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRI1->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRI1->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Disabled Channel
alarms.cause: I/O channel has been disabled.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action: Please check cables and HW connected to the I/O\nReenable the channel via the UI on the CPU module, once the problem has been fixed.\nReplace the module if the problem persists or if no problem external to the module is found.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRI1->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Module unavail.
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU*->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU*->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Disabled Channel
alarms.cause: I/O channel has been disabled.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action: Please check cables and HW connected to the I/O\nReenable the channel via the UI on the CPU module, once the problem has been fixed.\nReplace the module if the problem persists or if no problem external to the module is found.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU*->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Module unavail.
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->System->Packet loss monitor->Alarm->Packet loss detected
alarms.long_description: Packet loss detected within last minute.
alarms.cause: Network is not performing optimally.
alarms.effect: Communication between nodes is not working optimally.
alarms.suggested_action:
Please check network cables for bad connections.
The problem can be further isolated by using the Network Status screen:
1) Go to Maintenance -> Network Status
2) Press Status Views and select between any of the 4 Network Quality buttons
Network paths with lost packets observed within the last minute, last hour, last 24 hours or since last reset will then be indicated on the screen.

alarms.effect: ECS is unable to synchronize to the ship's clock.
alarms.suggested_action: Switch to internal clock in screen Admin - Set time\n2. Check communication cable.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU*->System->Modbus Interface->Modbus Slave failure
alarms.cause:
- Cable failure, or
- RCS failure, or
- EICU Modbus failure or
- Commissioning error
alarms.effect: If both EICUs report this alarm: RCS-ECS communication is lost. \nOnly hardwired control and monitoring is available (ECR/LOP)
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cabling
- RCS

If RCS and cabling is OK: Replace EICU

If both EICUs report this alarm: Restart RCS

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU*->System->Modbus Interface->Modbus Version->Modbus Interface Version Alarm
alarms.long_description: Modbus Interface Version does not match
alarms.cause: The Interface Version Number on the Modbus Master and Slave are different
alarms.effect: All data on the Modbus line is invalidated, until the Interface Version Number on Master and Slave side match.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Contact MAN-ES to retrieve the Interface Version Number for the specific plant.
- Check that the Interface Version Number for the specific plant is correct on the Master and Slave side.

RCS to ME-ECS Connections:
- If the Interface Version Number is not correct on the Master side please contact the RCS supplier for setting up the system correctly.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU*->System->Modbus Interface->Modbus Version->Modbus Configuration no. Alarm
alarms.long_description: The Configuration Number on the Modbus Master and Slave systems must be the same
alarms.cause: The Configuration Number on the Modbus Master and Slave is different
alarms.effect:
RCS to ME-ECS Connections:
- User interface on the RCS is set up based on the engine equipment and Engine Mode.
- Allowed commands and status fields are set up based on the Configuration Number.
Internal ME-ECS Modbus Connections:
- No Effect
alarms.suggested_action:
- Correct Parameters for Modbus Configuration

If problem persist:
Replace EICUA Controller or contact MAN-ES

Overriding:
 - Can cause hazardous situation and engine damage if used incorrectly!

 - Can cause or prevent duel SF stop or SF shut down.

alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.

alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action: Please check cables and HW connected to the I/O\nReenable the channel via the UI on the CPU module, once the problem has been fixed.\nReplace the module if the problem persists or if no problem external to the module is found.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU*->I/O Configuration->DR,2130-A,Cmd. Run. Dir. Ahead->2130-A-Cmd. Run. Dir. Ahead-Module unavail.
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:

2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

- Stop switch
- Analog handle signal and calibration

alarms.suggested_action: 1) Check on MOP screen: 'Maintenance' -> 'System View' which CCU's are missing or not operating in normal mode. \n2) Check for  problems with the network on MOP: Maintenance -> Network Status\n3) It can also be seen from the alarm list which CCU's cause the alarm.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU*->Supervision->Pump Control Supervision->Too many HP Pump Failures
alarms.long_description: Two or more high pressure pumps are failing
alarms.cause:
More than one high pressure pump cannot be controlled.

NOTE
If more than 3 pumps are installed, pump 4 and 5 are controlled by the ECUs
alarms.effect: - High pressure pumps move to fail safe position (maximum flow in ahead direction)\n- Reversing the engine may not be possible due to insufficient hydraulic pressure
alarms.suggested_action:
Check other alarms to locate the root cause for the pump alarms

NOTE
NEVER ignore this alarm. Safe critical issues may arise!

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU*->ECT Command interface->Commission Mode Req Active (Deviat
alarms.long_description: Deviation between the internal states of EICU A and EICU B regarding whether or not Shop Test Mode should be active.
alarms.cause: Deviation between the MOP commands received by EICU A and EICU B. Maybe due to one of the EICU's being offline when Shop Test Mode was enabled/disabled on the ECT screen.
alarms.effect: Redundancy reduced. In case of one of the EICU's going offline the ECS might make an abrupt change between Shop Test Mode / Not Shop Test Mode.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- EICU cabling

Reselect Shop Test Mode or Not Shop Test Mode on the ECT screen

If the problem persists:
- Restart either EICU A or EICU B when convenient

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU*->ECT Command interface->ECT Mode Act.(Limiters Increased)
alarms.cause: Shop Test Mode can be toggled on/off from the ECT application. When it is toggled on this alarm is active.
alarms.effect:
The following changes are in effect to allow necessary shop test trials to be carried out:
1: Max Engine Speed has been increased from 105% to 110% MCR
2: Overspeed protection limit change from 106% and 108% MCR to 110% MCR
3: P-scav and Torque limiters have been cancelled
4: Chief index limiter has been raised from 110% to 120%
5: The load program has been disabled
6: Chief Max Speed parameter has been disabled

Changes 1 and 3 are only in effect when ECR is the active control station.
alarms.suggested_action: It is ok for this alarm to be active during shop test when the ECT is being used for engine commissioning.\n\nBefore finishing shop test it is necessary to toggle Shop Test Mode to off via the ECT application.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->System->Packet loss monitor->Alarm->Packet loss detected
alarms.long_description: Packet loss detected within last minute.
alarms.cause: Network is not performing optimally.
alarms.effect: Communication between nodes is not working optimally.
alarms.suggested_action:
Please check network cables for bad connections.
The problem can be further isolated by using the Network Status screen:
1) Go to Maintenance -> Network Status
2) Press Status Views and select between any of the 4 Network Quality buttons
Network paths with lost packets observed within the last minute, last hour, last 24 hours or since last reset will then be indicated on the screen.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU->System->DR,SRELAY,Alarm relay Digital Out->SRELAY-Alarm relay Digital Out-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: OMCU->ACOM Control->High BN Tank->BN Outlet Valve->BN Valve Failure
alarms.long_description: High BN Valve position deviates from commanded position
alarms.cause: - Valve failure, or\n- Feedback failure, or\n- Cabling failure (Opened FB, Closed FB, Open Command)
alarms.effect: ACOM go to Failure Mode. ACOM Bypass Valve (ABV) Opens
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Valve
- Valve feedback
- Valve cabling (Opened FB, Closed FB, Open Command)

Further troubleshooting.
1. Operate valve by changing OMCU Controller mode to test. Avoid doing this while the engine is running.
2. Observe feedback during valve operation

alarms.data_tree_path: OMCU->ACOM Control->High BN Tank->Level Switch->Level Switch Dry
alarms.long_description: Level Switch in High BN tank is 'Dry'
alarms.cause:
- Signal Failure 
- Cable Failure 
- Supply from Day tank blocked by Manually Closed Inlet Valve or 
- Clogged Inlet Filter
alarms.effect: ACOM go to Failure Mode. ACOM Bypass Valve (ABV) Opens
alarms.suggested_action:
Check: 
- Cabling 
- Inlet Filter 
- Inlet Valve 
- If problem persists, replace level switch

alarms.data_tree_path: OMCU->ACOM Control->High BN Tank->Pump (VFD) Control->Setpoint Deviation Alarm
alarms.long_description: High BN Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) Speed Feedback deviates from Setpoint.
alarms.cause: Cabling Failure or\n- Scaling Tables Mismatch between ECS and OMCU
alarms.effect: ACOM go to Failure Mode. ACOM Bypass Valve (ABV) Opens
alarms.suggested_action: Check Cabling or Scaling of VFD

alarms.data_tree_path: OMCU->ACOM Control->High BN Tank->Pump (VFD) Control->Remote Local Fail Alarm
alarms.long_description: - Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) for High BN Tank is off or manually set to 'Local', or\n- Internal VFD Failure, or\n- Cabling failure
alarms.cause: - Operator has set VFD in Local Mode or\n- VFD Failure
alarms.effect: ACOM go to Failure Mode. ACOM Bypass Valve (ABV) Opens
alarms.suggested_action: - Check if VFD is set to 'Local' - switch back to 'Remote'. \n- If VFD is not set to 'Local' check local info on VFD monitor.\n- If no local alarm on VFD check cabling

alarms.data_tree_path: OMCU->ACOM Control->High BN Tank->Temperature Control->Temperature Sensor->Temperature Sensor Below Min
alarms.long_description: High BN Tank Temperature Below Minimum Allowed Value
alarms.cause: - Failing Heating Element, or \n- Failing Temperature Sensor
alarms.effect: ACOM continues normal operation. Temperature of BN Oil can be out of limits which may lead to incorrect mixing
alarms.suggested_action: Check: \n- Heating Element \n- Temperature Sensor

alarms.data_tree_path: OMCU->ACOM Control->High BN Tank->Temperature Control->Temperature Sensor->Temperature Sensor Above Max

alarms.suggested_action: Check: \n- Heating Element \n- Temperature Sensor

alarms.data_tree_path: OMCU->ACOM Control->High BN Tank->ACOM Bypass Valve->ABV Failure
alarms.long_description: Valve position deviates from commanded position
alarms.cause: - Valve failure, or\n- Feedback failure, or\n- Cabling failure (Opened FB, Closed FB, Open Command)
alarms.effect: ACOM go to Failure Mode. ACOM Bypass Valve (ABV) is commanded to Open. If stucked in: \n- Open position, high BN oil flows to mixing tank. \n- Closed position, no oil flow to mixing tank, which may lead to an engine slow-down
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Valve
- Valve feedback
- Actuator air supply
- Valve cabling (Opened FB, Closed FB, Open Command)

Further troubleshooting.
1. ABV is commanded to open. If stucked in closed position, try to open it manually.
2. Operate valve by changing OMCU Controller mode to test. Avoid doing this while the engine is running.
3. Observe feedback during valve operation.
