alarms.suggested_action: If this alarm occurs while the engine is in service please contact MAN-ES

alarms.data_tree_path: SACU2->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: SACU2->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Disabled Channel
alarms.cause: I/O channel has been disabled.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action: Please check cables and HW connected to the I/O\nReenable the channel via the UI on the CPU module, once the problem has been fixed.\nReplace the module if the problem persists or if no problem external to the module is found.

alarms.data_tree_path: SACU2->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Module unavail.
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

alarms.data_tree_path: SACU2->SPCU Com->No Telegram From SPCU
alarms.long_description: SACU2 did not receive a telegram network message from SPCU.
alarms.cause:
If SACU2 reports this alarm continuously:
- SPCU failure

If SACU2 reports this alarm randomly:
- Network failure
alarms.effect:
During dual fuel operation:
- Dual fuel stop
- Engine operation on fuel oil

During fuel oil operation:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable
alarms.suggested_action:
If SACU2 continues to report this alarm, check:
- SPCU
- Network cabling

If SACU2 randomly reports this failure, check:
- Network status. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Network Status'
- Network cabling and terminating resistors.
- For ground failure

alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->System->Watchdogs deactivated
alarms.cause: This alarm should not happen in Service
alarms.effect: No effect on engine performance. The SCRCU Controller may respond incorrectly to any software and hardware failures.
alarms.suggested_action: If this alarm occurs while the engine is in service please contact MAN-ES

alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Disabled Channel
alarms.cause: I/O channel has been disabled.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action: Please check cables and HW connected to the I/O\nReenable the channel via the UI on the CPU module, once the problem has been fixed.\nReplace the module if the problem persists or if no problem external to the module is found.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Module unavail.
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

alarms.cause:
- Cabling failure, or
- Sensor failure, or
- Supervision resistor across the switch is missing, or 
- SCRCU Controller input channel failure
alarms.effect: Reduced supervision. May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cabling
- Sensor
- Supervision resistor 
- SCRCU Controller input channel: 'Maintenance' -> 'System View I/O Test'

If the problem persists: Replace the corresponding module on SCRCU

alarms.synopsis: dp SCR Too High For Running SCR
alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->Supervision->HP SCR supervision->dp SCR supervision->dp SCR too high supervision->dp SCR Too High For Running SCR
alarms.long_description: Pressure difference over SCR line is too high for SCR to continue running.
alarms.cause: - Clogging of SCR reactor.\n- dp sensor failure.\n- SCR flow is restricted due to broken parts in the flow path.
alarms.effect: Automatic control will not be possible until the fault has been corrected.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check dp sensor.\n- Make a visual inspection of the SCR reactor, SCR flow path and SCR valves.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->Supervision->HP SCR supervision->dp SCR supervision->dp SCR too high supervision->dp SCR Too High
alarms.long_description: Pressure difference over SCR line is too high.
alarms.cause: - Clogging of SCR reactor.\n- dp sensor failure.\n- SCR flow is restricted due to broken parts in the flow path.
alarms.effect: If pressure difference over the SCR system is too high, the engine performance is reduced during SCR operation.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check dp sensor.
- Check in EMS that dp SCR has increased to the current too high level continuously, i.e. without any sudden jumps in the dp SCR value.

If the dp SCR value has increased continuously, load up the engine slowly to a high load, while manually monitoring the pressure measurements in the SCR line closely. This is done in order to regenerate the catalyst elements.

If the dp SCR value has increased by a sudden jump, check the status of the SCR reactor flow path.

alarms.long_description: The ABS limiter has attempted to force reducing agent dosing below minimum flow rate.
alarms.cause: - Pump supplying incorrectly large amounts of reducing agent.\n-  NOx sensor showing incorrectly low values.
alarms.effect: - Risk of ammonia slip.\n- Risk of ABS formation in SCR reactor.
alarms.suggested_action: - Make a bucket test to validate the dosing system is supplying the correct amount of urea.\n- Exchange NOx sensors.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->Supervision->General supervision->NOx sensor supervision->NOx sensors deviation supervision->NOx sensors deviating alarm
alarms.cause: - Malfunction of one or both NOx sensors.\n- Cabling.\n- NOx sensor temperature below Dew Point limit
alarms.effect: Reducing agent dosing rate might be affected.

 - Check NOx sensor temperature

alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->Supervision->General supervision->NOx sensor supervision->NOx sensor 1 ready supervision->NOx sensor 1 not ready
alarms.cause:
- NOx sensor failure.
- NOx sensor has not received NOx sensor ON signal.
 - NOx sensor temperature below Dew Point limit 
- Cable failure.
- SCR Control Sensor Unit failure. Note that PLC must be set in RUN and green light for CAN.
- SCRCU Controller failure.
alarms.effect: While alarm is present, this NOx sensor measurement is disregarded by ECS. Sensor redundancy is hence reduced.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Restart PLC in SCR Control Sensor Unit NOx cabinet on the circuit breaker Q1. 
 - Check NOx sensor temperature
- Check cabling and proper termination for CANbus.
- Check SCR Control Sensor Unit PLC module B3 input DI: 01. It must have a green light.
- Check SCR Control Sensor Unit PLC module B4 output DO: 01. It must have a green light.
- Check NOx sensor, replace if necessary. Make sure to exchange the sensor specifically mentioned in the alarm message and pay attention to replacing it with the correct sensor as the plugs are different between sensor 1 and 2. When replacing NOx sensors, the main breaker Q1 inside SCR NOx Cabinet should be switched OFF.
- Check SCRCU Controller.

alarms.long_description: NOx out of the SCR is higher than expected, hence the NOx reduction is too low.
alarms.cause:
- The entered reducing agent concentration is incorrect. 
- External dosing handling system is malfunctioning.
- Reducing agent injection nozzle is malfunctioning.
- The SCR catalyst has reduced conversion capacity.
- Leakage in the Reactor Bypass Valve.
- Mechanical damage to the SCR system.
alarms.effect: - Tier III NOx reduction active signal is disabled.\n- If failure persists the SCR system will be stopped.\n- Potentially unconverted reducing agent might result in ammonia slip and ABS downstream of the injection point.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check reducing agent concentration.
- Check external dosing handling system.
- Check reducing agent injection nozzle.
- Check SCR catalyst.
- Check for leakage in the Reactor Bypass Valve.
- Check for mechanical damages in SCR system.

alarms.long_description: SCR system is not ready for operation.
alarms.cause: - SCR Mode is Stop.\n- Failure in the SCR system.
alarms.effect: SCR system cannot start.\nStandby heat system will not run.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Remove cause of failure.
- Set SCR Mode in Auto on MOP.
- If engine is running: Manually close RTV and RSV.
- If engine is stopped and Engine Mode is Tier III: Manually close RTV and RSV and manually start Standby Heat system.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->Plant Control->System Control->Actuators in Manual Mode
alarms.long_description: SCR system actuators are in manual (possible when engine is stopped only).
alarms.cause: User switched SCR Mode to Manual.
alarms.effect: SCR system cannot switch to SCR Mode Auto.\nIf engine starts, SCR Mode will change to Stop.
alarms.suggested_action: Switch to SCR Mode Stop and then to SCR Mode Auto.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->Plant Control->Process State Machine->Flush Sequence Timed Out->Flush Sequence Timed Out
alarms.long_description: The external dosing handling system did not perform the dosing system flush sequence within the time limit.
alarms.cause: - Error in the flushing operation of the dosing handling system.\n- Error in cabling of signals between SCRCU Controller and external dosing handling system.
alarms.effect: The reactor will be disengaged.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check errors in external dosing handling system.\n- Check cabling of Run Dosing Sys. Flush Seq. and Dos Sys Flush Seq Running signals between SCRCU Controller and external dosing handling system.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->Plant Control->Process State Machine->Dosing Enabling Timed Out->Dosing Enabling Timed Out
alarms.long_description: The external dosing handling system did not set the Reducing Agent Injection Available signal high within the allowed time.
alarms.cause: - Internal error in the dosing handling system.\n- Cable error.
alarms.effect: - The dosing never starts, hence the NOx reduction does not start.\n- The reactor will be disengaged and SCR operation will not be possible until the fault has been corrected.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check the external dosing handling system.\n- Check cabling.

alarms.synopsis: p-SCR Too High, RTV will open
alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->Plant Control->Process Control->SCR Overpressure Control->RTV control->p-SCR Too High, RTV will open
alarms.long_description: RTV has opened due to too high pressure in SCR.
alarms.cause:
- Soot blowing system is leaking into the reactor.
- Venting system is leaking into the reactor.
- PEV malfunction.
- Cable failure.
alarms.effect: Exhaust/air with high pressure will be released from the SCR reactor into the TC and SCR bypass line. Risk of TC surging.\n\nMechanical/pneumatic safety dP opening of RSV/PEV is not affected and will ensure continued safety opening of RSV/PEV in case of too high over pressure in SCR system.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check status of turbocharger.
- Check status of soot blowing system.
- Check status of venting system.
- Check PEV.
- Check cabling.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->Valve Control->Valve Container->RTV->Valve Exercise Function->RTV Exercise Function Activated
alarms.cause: Automatic exercise function of valve is enabled.
alarms.effect: Valve position set point changed slightly for a short amount of time.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->Valve Control->Valve Container->RBV->Valve Exercise Function->RBV Exercise Function Activated
alarms.cause: Automatic exercise function of valve is enabled.
alarms.effect: Valve position set point changed slightly for a short amount of time.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->Valve Control->Valve Container->CBV->Valve Exercise Function->CBV Exercise Function Activated
alarms.cause: Automatic exercise function of valve is enabled.
alarms.effect: Valve position set point changed slightly for a short amount of time.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->Valve Control->Valve Control SM->SCR Line Min. Open timeout->SCR Line Min. Open timeout
alarms.long_description: The SCR line was opened partly, to stabilize the temperature measured by the temperature sensor SCR in, but the temperature did not reach a sufficient temperature for engaging SCR within the allowed time.
alarms.cause: - Temperature is to too low for SCR to engage.\n- Sensor failure.
alarms.effect: The reactor will be disengaged and SCR operation is disabled.
alarms.suggested_action: - Retry engagement of SCR at higher engine load.\n- Check the sensor.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->Valve Control->Valve Control SM->SCR Line Close timeout->SCR Line Close timeout
alarms.long_description: The SCR line did not close in the allowed time.
alarms.cause: - Valves RTV and/or RSV did not close in time.\n- Error in RTV and/or RSV valves.\n- Error in cabling.
alarms.effect: The SCR line might not be completely closed.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check RTV and RSV valves for errors.\n- Check cabling of RTV and RSV set point and feedback signals.\n- Manually close RTV and RSV, if required.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->Dosing Control->Simplified Specific NOx Estimate->Scavenge Air O2->O2 conc. scav. too low
alarms.long_description: O2 concentration in scavenging air receiver calculated from ambient temperature, relative humidity, ambient pressure and scavenging temperature is below 19.0%
alarms.cause: - Sensor Error \n- Cabling Error
alarms.effect: - No valid SSN Value
alarms.suggested_action: - Check O2 sensors \n- Check Cabling

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->System->Watchdogs deactivated
alarms.cause: This alarm should not happen in Service
alarms.effect: No effect on engine performance. \nThe SCSU1 Controller may respond incorrectly to any software and hardware failures.
alarms.suggested_action: If this alarm occurs while the engine is in service please contact MAN-ES

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Disabled Channel
alarms.cause: I/O channel has been disabled.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action: Please check cables and HW connected to the I/O\nReenable the channel via the UI on the CPU module, once the problem has been fixed.\nReplace the module if the problem persists or if no problem external to the module is found.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Module unavail.
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->IO Configuration->Tacho->Missing TIU-A and TIU-B telegram
alarms.long_description: Missing network telegram message from both TIUA and TIUB
alarms.cause: TIUA and TIUB are not transmitting or\nThe TIUA/TIUB or SCSU1 Controller network connection may be broken.\nCould also be a network switch failure
alarms.effect: TheSCSU1 Controller due to no reception of engine information (speed, position and direction)
alarms.suggested_action:
If the alarm continues to stay active while engine runs, check: 
- Both TIU Controllers are powered on and LEDs indicates correct status
- Check switch LED status
- Network cabling between the TIU Controllers and switch
- Network cabling between the SCSU1 Controller and switch

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->IO Configuration->Tacho->Missing TIU-A telegram
alarms.long_description: Missing network telegram message from TIUA
alarms.cause: TIUA and TIUB are not transmitting or\nThe TIUA/TIUB or SCSU1 Controller network connection may be broken.\nCould also be a network switch failure
alarms.effect:
No redundant reception of engine information (speed, position and direction).
If both TIU telegrams are missing on same SCSU1 Controller:
- No fuel injection on that unit
- No cylinder lubrication
- No exhaust valve movement
alarms.suggested_action:
If the alarm continues to stay active while engine runs, check: 
- Both TIU Controllers are powered on and LEDs indicates correct status
- Check switch LED status
- Network cabling between the TIU Controllers and switch
- Network cabling between the SCSU1 Controller and switch

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->IO Configuration->Tacho->Missing TIU-B telegram
alarms.long_description: Missing network telegram message from TIUB
alarms.cause: TIUB is not transmitting or The TIUA or SCSU1 Controller network connection may be broken. Could also be switch failure
alarms.effect:
No redundant reception of engine information (speed, position and direction).
If both TIU telegrams are missing on same SCSU1 Controller:
- No fuel injection on that unit
- No cylinder lubrication
- No exhaust valve movement
alarms.suggested_action:
If the alarm continues to stay active while engine runs, check: 
- Both TIU Controllers are powered on and LEDs indicates correct status
- Check switch LED status
- Network cabling between the TIU Controllers and switch
- Network cabling between the SCSU1 Controller and switch

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->IO Configuration->Tacho->Tacho Sys. ATC setup rejected
alarms.cause: Internal timing margin too small
alarms.effect: One Injection or exhaust valve closure might have been skipped. The controller will continue normal operation.
alarms.suggested_action: Please contact MAN-ES

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->IO Configuration->AI,6332-B,Outer Pipe HC B (LEL)->6332-B-Outer Pipe HC B (LEL)-No Connection
alarms.cause:
- Cabling failure, or
- Sensor failure, or
- Supervision resistor across the switch is missing, or 
- SCSU1 Controller input channel failure
alarms.effect:
During dual fuel operation:
- Dual fuel shutdown
- Engine operation on fuel oil

During fuel oil operation:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cabling
- Sensor
- Supervision resistor 
- SCSU1 Controller input channel: 'Maintenance' -> 'System View I/O Test'

If the problem persists: Replace the corresponding module on SCSU1

alarms.long_description: AI or 'DI by Analog' Channel overload.
alarms.cause: Cabling and/or sensor issue.
alarms.effect: Signal value is outside the safe range of the Channel and cannot be measured.\nMay reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action: Please check cabling and/or sensor..

alarms.suggested_action: Please check cables and HW connected to the I/O\nReenable the channel via the UI on the CPU module, once the problem has been fixed.\nReplace the module if the problem persists or if no problem external to the module is found.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU->IO Configuration->DO,6430-C,ELGI/ELGA Enable->6430-C-ELGI/ELGA Enable-Module unavail.
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 1: Supervision->Cyl 1: Second fuel blocked
alarms.long_description: Second fuel operation on cylinder 1 is blocked
alarms.cause:
SCSU cylinder supervision has detected a situation, which may potentially damage the engine if not treated correctly.
- Cylinder pressure supervision has detected too high max pressure or too fast pressure rise, or
- GI engines: SF channel pressure supervision has detected SF pressure drop test failure, SF pressure curve fit failure or SF pressure range failure.
- LGI engines: SF channel pressure sensor has detected a leaking FBIV sliding- and suction-valves
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable, 
- Manual assembly test and manual purge of second fuel system is unavailable.


WARNING!
Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
RECOMMENDATION if leaking SF injection valve:
- Cut-out fuel oil injection on this cylinder, or 
- Stop and exchange the damaged valve.

DO NOT start dual fuel operation until this failure is located and repaired.

DO NOT reset second fuel block before failure is located.

Check:
- Other alarms stating cause of SF shutdown and recommended action
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.

If failure is identified as a missing pilot, adjust pilot injection and reset second fuel blocked.

If another failure is located in second fuel system, perform troubleshooting on second fuel block with stopped engine before reset of second fuel block.

To reset second fuel block, go to: 'Engine'->'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' and reset 'Second Fuel Block'.

alarms.effect: - Blow back from combustion chamber into the injector\n- Injector may be damaged by the combustion gas pressure pulsations\n- SF injector becomes hot
alarms.suggested_action: - Stop engine and replace SF injection valve

- Second fuel blocked

Check:

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 1: Supervision->Cyl 1: Alarms->Cyl 1: ELBI Feedback Failure
alarms.long_description: ELBI Closed sensor deviates from ELBI Valve Command signal
alarms.cause:
- ELBI Closed sensor failure
- ELBI Valve failure (closes to slowly or does not close)
- Cabling failure on command signal or feedback signal
- Excessive noise on feedback signal
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel shutdown\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action:
Check: 
- Cabling (command or feedback)
- ELBI Valve
- ELBI Closed Sensor
- Use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder

If problem persists:
1. Operate valve by changing SCSU mode to test.
2. Observe feedback during valve operation

If command and feedback match, the ELBI feedback sensor is possibly too slow and must be replaced.

If command and feedback do not match, either the ELBI Feedback sensor is failing or the ELBI Valve is failing and one or both must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 2: Supervision->Cyl 2: Second fuel blocked
alarms.long_description: Second fuel operation on cylinder 2 is blocked
alarms.cause:
SCSU cylinder supervision has detected a situation, which may potentially damage the engine if not treated correctly.
- Cylinder pressure supervision has detected too high max pressure or too fast pressure rise, or
- GI engines: SF channel pressure supervision has detected SF pressure drop test failure, SF pressure curve fit failure or SF pressure range failure.
- LGI engines: SF channel pressure sensor has detected a leaking FBIV sliding- and suction-valves
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable, 
- Manual assembly test and manual purge of second fuel system is unavailable.


WARNING!
Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
RECOMMENDATION if leaking SF injection valve:
- Cut-out fuel oil injection on this cylinder, or 
- Stop and exchange the damaged valve.

DO NOT start dual fuel operation until this failure is located and repaired.

DO NOT reset second fuel block before failure is located.

Check:
- Other alarms stating cause of SF shutdown and recommended action
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.

If failure is identified as a missing pilot, adjust pilot injection and reset second fuel blocked.

If another failure is located in second fuel system, perform troubleshooting on second fuel block with stopped engine before reset of second fuel block.

To reset second fuel block, go to: 'Engine'->'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' and reset 'Second Fuel Block'.

- ELBI Valve

alarms.effect:

- Excessive noise on feedback signal
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel shutdown\n- Engine operation on fuel oil

Check: 
- Cabling (command or feedback)
- ELBI Valve
- ELBI Closed Sensor
- Use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder

If problem persists:
1. Operate valve by changing SCSU mode to test.
2. Observe feedback during valve operation

If command and feedback match, the ELBI feedback sensor is possibly too slow and must be replaced.

If command and feedback do not match, either the ELBI Feedback sensor is failing or the ELBI Valve is failing and one or both must be replaced.

- Cylinder pressure supervision has detected too high max pressure or too fast pressure rise, or
- GI engines: SF channel pressure supervision has detected SF pressure drop test failure, SF pressure curve fit failure or SF pressure range failure.
- LGI engines: SF channel pressure sensor has detected a leaking FBIV sliding- and suction-valves
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable, 
- Manual assembly test and manual purge of second fuel system is unavailable.


WARNING!
Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!

- Stop and exchange the damaged valve.

DO NOT start dual fuel operation until this failure is located and repaired.

DO NOT reset second fuel block before failure is located.

Check:
- Other alarms stating cause of SF shutdown and recommended action
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.

If failure is identified as a missing pilot, adjust pilot injection and reset second fuel blocked.

If another failure is located in second fuel system, perform troubleshooting on second fuel block with stopped engine before reset of second fuel block.

To reset second fuel block, go to: 'Engine'->'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' and reset 'Second Fuel Block'.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 4: Supervision->Cyl 4: Alarms->Cyl 4: ELBI Feedback Failure
alarms.long_description: ELBI Closed sensor deviates from ELBI Valve Command signal
alarms.cause:
- ELBI Closed sensor failure
- ELBI Valve failure (closes to slowly or does not close)
- Cabling failure on command signal or feedback signal
- Excessive noise on feedback signal
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel shutdown\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action:
Check: 
- Cabling (command or feedback)
- ELBI Valve
- ELBI Closed Sensor
- Use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder

If problem persists:
1. Operate valve by changing SCSU mode to test.
2. Observe feedback during valve operation

If command and feedback match, the ELBI feedback sensor is possibly too slow and must be replaced.

If command and feedback do not match, either the ELBI Feedback sensor is failing or the ELBI Valve is failing and one or both must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 5: Supervision->Cyl 5: Second fuel blocked
alarms.long_description: Second fuel operation on cylinder 5 is blocked
alarms.cause:
SCSU cylinder supervision has detected a situation, which may potentially damage the engine if not treated correctly.
- Cylinder pressure supervision has detected too high max pressure or too fast pressure rise, or
- GI engines: SF channel pressure supervision has detected SF pressure drop test failure, SF pressure curve fit failure or SF pressure range failure.
- LGI engines: SF channel pressure sensor has detected a leaking FBIV sliding- and suction-valves
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable, 
- Manual assembly test and manual purge of second fuel system is unavailable.


WARNING!
Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
RECOMMENDATION if leaking SF injection valve:
- Cut-out fuel oil injection on this cylinder, or 
- Stop and exchange the damaged valve.

DO NOT start dual fuel operation until this failure is located and repaired.

DO NOT reset second fuel block before failure is located.

Check:
- Other alarms stating cause of SF shutdown and recommended action
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.

If failure is identified as a missing pilot, adjust pilot injection and reset second fuel blocked.

If another failure is located in second fuel system, perform troubleshooting on second fuel block with stopped engine before reset of second fuel block.

To reset second fuel block, go to: 'Engine'->'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' and reset 'Second Fuel Block'.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU->IO Configuration->DR,6428-D,SF ELFI Enable->6428-D-SF ELFI Enable-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU->IO Configuration->DR,6428-D,SF ELFI Enable->6428-D-SF ELFI Enable-Disabled Channel
alarms.cause: I/O channel has been disabled.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action: Please check cables and HW connected to the I/O\nReenable the channel via the UI on the CPU module, once the problem has been fixed.\nReplace the module if the problem persists or if no problem external to the module is found.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU->IO Configuration->DR,6428-D,SF ELFI Enable->6428-D-SF ELFI Enable-Module unavail.
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 9: Supervision->Cyl 9: Second fuel blocked
alarms.long_description: Second fuel operation on cylinder 9 is blocked
alarms.cause:
SCSU cylinder supervision has detected a situation, which may potentially damage the engine if not treated correctly.
- Cylinder pressure supervision has detected too high max pressure or too fast pressure rise, or
- GI engines: SF channel pressure supervision has detected SF pressure drop test failure, SF pressure curve fit failure or SF pressure range failure.
- LGI engines: SF channel pressure sensor has detected a leaking FBIV sliding- and suction-valves
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable, 
- Manual assembly test and manual purge of second fuel system is unavailable.


WARNING!
Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
RECOMMENDATION if leaking SF injection valve:
- Cut-out fuel oil injection on this cylinder, or 
- Stop and exchange the damaged valve.

DO NOT start dual fuel operation until this failure is located and repaired.

DO NOT reset second fuel block before failure is located.

Check:
- Other alarms stating cause of SF shutdown and recommended action
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.

If failure is identified as a missing pilot, adjust pilot injection and reset second fuel blocked.

If another failure is located in second fuel system, perform troubleshooting on second fuel block with stopped engine before reset of second fuel block.

To reset second fuel block, go to: 'Engine'->'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' and reset 'Second Fuel Block'.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 9: Supervision->Cyl 9: SF Inj Valve Leaking
alarms.long_description: SF injection valve is leaking when running on fuel oil or in SF standby
alarms.cause: - Seizing of injection valve \n- Particles prevent closing the valve completely
alarms.effect: - Blow back from combustion chamber into the injector\n- Injector may be damaged by the combustion gas pressure pulsations\n- SF injector becomes hot
alarms.suggested_action: - Stop engine and replace SF injection valve

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 9: Supervision->Cyl 9: Invalid Superv. Limits
alarms.long_description: Cylinder supervision test limits could not be calculated
alarms.cause: - Missing communication from CCU\n- Invalid input data from CCU\n- Invalid supervision parameters
alarms.effect:
During dual fuel operation:
- Dual fuel shutdown
- Engine operation on fuel oil

During fuel oil operation:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Alarm list for missing telegrams

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 9: Supervision->Cyl 9: No Telegram from CCU
alarms.long_description: SCSU did not receive a telegram network message from CCU.\n\nTelegram is sent from CCU once per revolution, after receiving fuel telegram, and contains information about engine speed, fuel indexes and injection timing etc.
alarms.cause:
If SCSU reports this alarm continuously:
- CCU failure

If SCSU reports this alarm randomly:
- Network failure
- Tacho A failure
- SCSU controller overload
alarms.effect:
During dual fuel operation:
- Dual fuel shutdown
- Engine operation on fuel oil

During fuel oil operation:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable
alarms.suggested_action:
If SCSU continues to report this alarm, check: 
- CCU
- Network cabling

If SCSU randomly reports this failure, check:
- Network status. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Network Status'
- Network cabling and terminating resistors.
- For earth fault

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 9: Supervision->Cyl 9: Alarms->Cyl 9: Compress Press Too Low
alarms.long_description: Compression pressure is too low for SF injection.
alarms.cause:
- Leaking exhaust valve, or 
- Piston ring blow-by, or
- Air spring failure, or 
- Exhaust valve actuator failure, or 
- Exhaust valve damper failure, or  
- ELFI / FIVA valve failure, or
- Pcomp/Pscav offset, or
- Cylinder pressure sensor failure
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel shutdown\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cylinder pressure. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events'
- Alarms on MOP
- Exhaust valve closing. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU Events'
- Air spring
- Exhaust valve actuator
- Exhaust valve oil cylinder
- ELFI / FIVA valve
- Pcomp/Pscav offset adjustments

Check on PMI:
- Cylinder pressure sensor signal

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 9: Supervision->Cyl 9: Alarms->Cyl 9: Max Press Too High
alarms.long_description: Cylinder pressure exceeds maximum allowed pressure
alarms.cause: - Too early injection of fuel oil or second fuel caused by engine process adjustments, or\n- GI engines: ELGI valve stuck in open position
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel shutdown
- Engine operation on fuel oil
- Second fuel blocked

WARNING! (GI engines)
Ignoring an ELGI valve stuck in open position will result in damage to SF injection valve, causing it to leak.

Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.
- Engine process adjustments, go to 'Engine' -> 'Process Adjustment' -> 'Cylinder Press.' 
- Index calibration mode must be auto for dual fuel operation, go to 'Engine' -> 'Process Adjustment' -> 'Index Calibration' 

WARNING! (GI engines)
If second fuel pressure curve is abnormal (injection starts early when WV is activated or pressure drop is higher than normal), do not attempt to restart dual fuel operation, before engine has been stopped and gas block troubleshooting is completed. Go to 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Gas Block'.

Reference is made to circular letter or instruction manual showing pressure curves from typical failure situation.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 9: Supervision->Cyl 9: Alarms->Cyl 9: Expansion Press Too Low
alarms.long_description: Cylinder expansion pressure is lower than expected
alarms.cause:
- Missing fuel oil injection, or
- Missing second fuel injection, or
- Misfiring, or
- Lower calorific value of sec fuel is too low, or
- Cylinder pressure sensor failure

Missing SF injection can be caused by:
- ELGI/ELFI-L valve failure, or
- Second fuel injection valve failure, or
- ELWI/ELBI valve failure
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel shutdown\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events'
- Alarms on MOP
- Fuel plunger timing and movement. Go to: 'MOP B' -> 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU Events'. 
- Look for ELFI enable signal on 'HCU Events'. 

Check on PMI:
- Cylinder pressure sensor signal. 
- Observe other alarms that might be the cause of the shutdown. Investigate the different possible scenarios

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 9: Supervision->Cyl 9: Alarms->Cyl 9: Expansion Press Too High
alarms.long_description: Cylinder expansion pressure is higher than expected
alarms.cause: - Too much Second fuel injected or\n- Too much fuel oil injected

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 10: Supervision->Cyl 10: Alarms->Cyl 10: ELBI Feedback Failure
alarms.long_description: ELBI Closed sensor deviates from ELBI Valve Command signal
alarms.cause:
- ELBI Closed sensor failure
- ELBI Valve failure (closes to slowly or does not close)
- Cabling failure on command signal or feedback signal
- Excessive noise on feedback signal
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel shutdown\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action:
Check: 
- Cabling (command or feedback)
- ELBI Valve
- ELBI Closed Sensor
- Use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder

If problem persists:
1. Operate valve by changing SCSU mode to test.
2. Observe feedback during valve operation

If command and feedback match, the ELBI feedback sensor is possibly too slow and must be replaced.

If command and feedback do not match, either the ELBI Feedback sensor is failing or the ELBI Valve is failing and one or both must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 11: Supervision->Cyl 11: Second fuel blocked
alarms.long_description: Second fuel operation on cylinder 11 is blocked
alarms.cause:
SCSU cylinder supervision has detected a situation, which may potentially damage the engine if not treated correctly.
- Cylinder pressure supervision has detected too high max pressure or too fast pressure rise, or
- GI engines: SF channel pressure supervision has detected SF pressure drop test failure, SF pressure curve fit failure or SF pressure range failure.
- LGI engines: SF channel pressure sensor has detected a leaking FBIV sliding- and suction-valves
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable, 
- Manual assembly test and manual purge of second fuel system is unavailable.


WARNING!
Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
RECOMMENDATION if leaking SF injection valve:
- Cut-out fuel oil injection on this cylinder, or 
- Stop and exchange the damaged valve.

DO NOT start dual fuel operation until this failure is located and repaired.

DO NOT reset second fuel block before failure is located.

Check:
- Other alarms stating cause of SF shutdown and recommended action
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.

If failure is identified as a missing pilot, adjust pilot injection and reset second fuel blocked.

If another failure is located in second fuel system, perform troubleshooting on second fuel block with stopped engine before reset of second fuel block.

To reset second fuel block, go to: 'Engine'->'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' and reset 'Second Fuel Block'.

alarms.cause: - SF injection valve leaking causing too large SF injection and blow back from combustion chamber, or\n- Window/Resume (if present) valve leaking causing SF flow from accumulator to SF channel, or\n- Blow off valve leaking
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel shutdown
- Engine operation on fuel oil
- Second fuel blocked

WARNING!
Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
RECOMMENDATION if leaking SF injection valve:
- Cut-out fuel oil injection on this cylinder, or 
- Stop and exchange the damaged valve.

DO NOT start dual fuel operation until this failure is located and repaired.

DO NOT reset second fuel block before failure is located.

Check:
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.
- Window valve
- Second fuel injection valve

WARNING! (GI engines)
If second fuel pressure curve is abnormal (injection starts early when WV is activated or pressure drop is higher than normal), do not attempt to restart dual fuel operation, before engine has been stopped and gas block troubleshooting is completed. Go to 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Gas Block'.

Reference is made to circular letter or instruction manual showing pressure curves from typical failure situation.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 11: Supervision->Cyl 11: Alarms->Cyl 11: ELBI Feedback Failure
alarms.long_description: ELBI Closed sensor deviates from ELBI Valve Command signal
alarms.cause:
- ELBI Closed sensor failure
- ELBI Valve failure (closes to slowly or does not close)
- Cabling failure on command signal or feedback signal
- Excessive noise on feedback signal
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel shutdown\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action:
Check: 
- Cabling (command or feedback)
- ELBI Valve
- ELBI Closed Sensor
- Use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder

If problem persists:
1. Operate valve by changing SCSU mode to test.
2. Observe feedback during valve operation

If command and feedback match, the ELBI feedback sensor is possibly too slow and must be replaced.

If command and feedback do not match, either the ELBI Feedback sensor is failing or the ELBI Valve is failing and one or both must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 12: Supervision->Cyl 12: Second fuel blocked
alarms.long_description: Second fuel operation on cylinder 12 is blocked
alarms.cause:
SCSU cylinder supervision has detected a situation, which may potentially damage the engine if not treated correctly.
- Cylinder pressure supervision has detected too high max pressure or too fast pressure rise, or
- GI engines: SF channel pressure supervision has detected SF pressure drop test failure, SF pressure curve fit failure or SF pressure range failure.
- LGI engines: SF channel pressure sensor has detected a leaking FBIV sliding- and suction-valves
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable, 
- Manual assembly test and manual purge of second fuel system is unavailable.


WARNING!
Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
RECOMMENDATION if leaking SF injection valve:
- Cut-out fuel oil injection on this cylinder, or 
- Stop and exchange the damaged valve.

DO NOT start dual fuel operation until this failure is located and repaired.

DO NOT reset second fuel block before failure is located.

Check:
- Other alarms stating cause of SF shutdown and recommended action
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.

If failure is identified as a missing pilot, adjust pilot injection and reset second fuel blocked.

If another failure is located in second fuel system, perform troubleshooting on second fuel block with stopped engine before reset of second fuel block.

To reset second fuel block, go to: 'Engine'->'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' and reset 'Second Fuel Block'.

alarms.effect: - Dual fuel shutdown\n- Engine operation on fuel oil

Check on PMI:
- Cylinder pressure sensor signal.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 12: Supervision->Cyl 12: Alarms->Cyl 12: ELBI Feedback Failure
alarms.long_description: ELBI Closed sensor deviates from ELBI Valve Command signal
alarms.cause:
- ELBI Closed sensor failure
- ELBI Valve failure (closes to slowly or does not close)
- Cabling failure on command signal or feedback signal
- Excessive noise on feedback signal
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel shutdown\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action:
Check: 
- Cabling (command or feedback)
- ELBI Valve
- ELBI Closed Sensor
- Use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder

If problem persists:
1. Operate valve by changing SCSU mode to test.
2. Observe feedback during valve operation

If command and feedback match, the ELBI feedback sensor is possibly too slow and must be replaced.

If command and feedback do not match, either the ELBI Feedback sensor is failing or the ELBI Valve is failing and one or both must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 13: Supervision->Cyl 13: Second fuel blocked
alarms.long_description: Second fuel operation on cylinder 13 is blocked
alarms.cause:
SCSU cylinder supervision has detected a situation, which may potentially damage the engine if not treated correctly.
- Cylinder pressure supervision has detected too high max pressure or too fast pressure rise, or
- GI engines: SF channel pressure supervision has detected SF pressure drop test failure, SF pressure curve fit failure or SF pressure range failure.
- LGI engines: SF channel pressure sensor has detected a leaking FBIV sliding- and suction-valves
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable, 
- Manual assembly test and manual purge of second fuel system is unavailable.


WARNING!
Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
RECOMMENDATION if leaking SF injection valve:
- Cut-out fuel oil injection on this cylinder, or 
- Stop and exchange the damaged valve.

DO NOT start dual fuel operation until this failure is located and repaired.

DO NOT reset second fuel block before failure is located.

Check:
- Other alarms stating cause of SF shutdown and recommended action
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.

If failure is identified as a missing pilot, adjust pilot injection and reset second fuel blocked.

If another failure is located in second fuel system, perform troubleshooting on second fuel block with stopped engine before reset of second fuel block.

To reset second fuel block, go to: 'Engine'->'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' and reset 'Second Fuel Block'.

Check: 
- Cabling (command or feedback)
- ELBI Valve
- ELBI Closed Sensor
- Use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder

2. Observe feedback during valve operation

alarms.effect:

alarms.effect:

WARNING!

alarms.cause: - SF injection valve leaking causing too large SF injection and blow back from combustion chamber, or\n- Window/Resume (if present) valve leaking causing SF flow from accumulator to SF channel, or\n- Blow off valve leaking
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel shutdown
- Engine operation on fuel oil
- Second fuel blocked

WARNING!
Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
RECOMMENDATION if leaking SF injection valve:
- Cut-out fuel oil injection on this cylinder, or 
- Stop and exchange the damaged valve.

DO NOT start dual fuel operation until this failure is located and repaired.

DO NOT reset second fuel block before failure is located.

Check:
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.
- Window valve
- Second fuel injection valve

WARNING! (GI engines)
If second fuel pressure curve is abnormal (injection starts early when WV is activated or pressure drop is higher than normal), do not attempt to restart dual fuel operation, before engine has been stopped and gas block troubleshooting is completed. Go to 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Gas Block'.

Reference is made to circular letter or instruction manual showing pressure curves from typical failure situation.

Check:
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.

Reference is made to circular letter or instruction manual showing pressure curves from typical failure situation.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 16: Supervision->Cyl 16: Alarms->Cyl 16: ELBI Feedback Failure
alarms.long_description: ELBI Closed sensor deviates from ELBI Valve Command signal
alarms.cause:
- ELBI Closed sensor failure
- ELBI Valve failure (closes to slowly or does not close)
- Cabling failure on command signal or feedback signal
- Excessive noise on feedback signal
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel shutdown\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action:
Check: 
- Cabling (command or feedback)
- ELBI Valve
- ELBI Closed Sensor
- Use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder

If problem persists:
1. Operate valve by changing SCSU mode to test.
2. Observe feedback during valve operation

If command and feedback match, the ELBI feedback sensor is possibly too slow and must be replaced.

If command and feedback do not match, either the ELBI Feedback sensor is failing or the ELBI Valve is failing and one or both must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: SPCU->System->Watchdogs deactivated
alarms.cause: This alarm should not happen in Service
alarms.effect: No effect on engine performance. \nThe SPCU Controller may respond incorrectly to any software and hardware failures.
alarms.suggested_action: If this alarm occurs while the engine is in service please contact MAN-ES

alarms.data_tree_path: SPCU->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: SPCU->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Disabled Channel
alarms.cause: I/O channel has been disabled.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action: Please check cables and HW connected to the I/O\nReenable the channel via the UI on the CPU module, once the problem has been fixed.\nReplace the module if the problem persists or if no problem external to the module is found.

alarms.data_tree_path: SPCU->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Module unavail.
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

alarms.data_tree_path: SPCU->SFCB: Cylinder Block->Second Fuel Blocked
alarms.long_description: Second Fuel Injection on one or more cylinders is blocked
alarms.cause:
SCSU cylinder supervision has detected a situation, which may potentially damage the engine if not treated correctly.
- Cylinder pressure supervision has detected too high max pressure or too fast pressure rise, or
- GI engines: SF channel pressure supervision has detected SF pressure drop test failure, SF pressure curve fit failure or SF pressure range failure.
- LGI engines: SF channel pressure sensor has detected a leaking FBIV sliding- and suction-valves
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable, 
- Manual assembly test and manual purge of second fuel system is unavailable.


WARNING!
Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
RECOMMENDATION if leaking SF injection valve:
- Cut-out fuel oil injection on this cylinder, or 
- Stop and exchange the damaged valve.

DO NOT start dual fuel operation until this failure is located and repaired.

DO NOT reset second fuel block before failure is located.

Check:
- Other alarms stating cause of SF shutdown and recommended action
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.

If failure is identified as a missing pilot, adjust pilot injection and reset second fuel blocked.

If another failure is located in second fuel system, perform troubleshooting on second fuel block with stopped engine before reset of second fuel block.

To reset second fuel block, go to: 'Engine'->'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' and reset 'Second Fuel Block'.

alarms.long_description: Pressure detected in second fuel channel
alarms.cause:
ME-GA:
- Cylinder blocked, blow off not possible on affected cylinder
- Window valve failure (blow off failure)
- !!! WARNING !!! A leaking GAV may cause pressure buildup during fuel oil operation!

LGIP:
- Pressure buildup due to vaporization if manual inlet and outlet valves are closed

LGIM:
- Blow off valve failure causing pressure increase due to vaporization

General:
- Second fuel channel pressure sensor malfunction
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel operation unavailable\n- Maintenance on second fuel system on engine not allowed!
alarms.suggested_action:
ME-GA:
If cylinder was blocked during blow off, refer to other alarms first, then:
- Go to: 'Auxiliaries' -> 'Second Fuel System' -> 'SF Pipes' -> 'Plant State'. Enter and then exit Manual Mode to trigger automatic depressurization through window and bleed valves.
- Alternatively, SGAV can be depressurized to outer pipe by opening manual relief plug.

If leaking GAV is suspected:
- Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to identify if there are pressure fluctuations in SGAV due to leaking GAV.

RECOMMENDATION

If leaking GAV:
- Cut-out fuel oil injection on this cylinder, or
- Stop and exchange the damaged valve.

DO NOT attempt to start dual fuel operation until this failure is located and repaired.


LGIP:
- Depressurize second fuel cylinder blocks by opening manual inlet/outlet valves

LGIM:
- Go to: 'Auxiliaries' -> 'Second Fuel System' -> 'SF Pipes' -> 'Plant State'. Enter and then exit Manual Mode to trigger automatic depressurization through ELBI.

General:
- Check second fuel channel pressure sensor

alarms.effect:
During dual fuel operation:
- Dual fuel shutdown
- Engine operation on fuel oil

During fuel oil operation:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: SPSU->IO Configuration->DI,6073,SFRVT Bleed Valve Open Sw->6073-SFRVT Bleed Valve Open Sw-Module unavail.
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect:
During dual fuel operation:
- Dual fuel shutdown
- Engine operation on fuel oil

During fuel oil operation:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

- Engine operation on fuel oil

alarms.data_tree_path: SPSU->SAFE: Plant Safety->Seal Oil Pressure Low
alarms.long_description: The differential pressure between sec fuel pressure and seal oil pressure is too low.

- Seal oil system leakage, or
- Seal oil pressure sensor failure, or

- Seal oil system
- Alarm for high second fuel pressure
- Seal oil filter

1. Start seal oil pump
2. Check seal oil pressure sensors

alarms.data_tree_path: SPSU->SAFE: Plant Safety->SF Inlet Pressure Too Low
alarms.long_description: Second fuel inlet pressure too low
alarms.cause:
- Second fuel supply system failure, or
- second fuel inlet pressure sensor failure, or
- If present: Second fuel flow restriction valve failure, or
- If present: Gas Regulator Unit failure
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel shutdown\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Second fuel inlet pressure sensor
- Second fuel supply system
- If present: Gas Regulator Unit
- If present: Second fuel flow restriction valve
Further troubleshooting.
1. Operate second fuel flow restriction valve by changing SPSU Controller mode to test
2. Observe valve operation, as valve is unsupervised

alarms.data_tree_path: SPSU->SAFE: Plant Safety->SF Pressure Too High

 Check:
 - Second fuel supply system pressure sensor
 - Second fuel inlet pressure sensor

 - Second fuel supply system

alarms.data_tree_path: SPSU->SAFE: Plant Safety->SF Blow Off Failure
alarms.long_description: Second fuel inlet pressure too high after blow off.
alarms.cause: - Second fuel purge valves failure, or\n- Second fuel inlet pressure sensor failure
alarms.effect: - Second fuel system may still be pressurised
alarms.suggested_action:

- Purge valves
- Sec fuel inlet pressure sensor
If second fuel pipes on engine are depressurized release state lock by invalidating Second Fuel Inlet Pressure sensor

alarms.data_tree_path: SPSU->SAFE: Plant Safety->Outer Pipe Ventilation Flow Low

- Double pipe outer pipe leakage, or

- Sensor failure

During dual fuel operation:
- Dual fuel shutdown
- Engine operation on fuel oil

During fuel oil operation:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable
alarms.suggested_action:

- Safety outer pipe ventilation flow sensor
- Double pipe

1. Start outer pipe ventilation in local control
2. Check outer pipe ventilation outlet flow or inlet suction
3. Check flow sensors. Go to: Second fuel system' -> 'Outer pipe'

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU*->System->Watchdogs deactivated
alarms.cause: This alarm should not happen in Service
alarms.effect: No effect on engine performance. \nThe TIUA Controller may respond incorrectly to any software and hardware failures.
alarms.suggested_action: If this alarm occurs while the engine is in service please contact MAN-ES

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU*->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU*->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Disabled Channel
alarms.cause: I/O channel has been disabled.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action: Please check cables and HW connected to the I/O\nReenable the channel via the UI on the CPU module, once the problem has been fixed.\nReplace the module if the problem persists or if no problem external to the module is found.

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU*->System->PPS Signal->DO,PPSDO,Pulse Per Second DO->PPSDO-Pulse Per Second DO-Module unavail.
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU*->TIU manager->Dual Tacho->Dual tacho marker trig missing
alarms.cause: Defect wiring, sensors, encoders or sensor support console.
alarms.effect: The controller had to change active tacho encoder set. \nIn case both dual tacho sensor sets are invalid on TIUA and TIUB, dual tacho functionality will be lost. \nEngine speed hunting may occur while the problem is active.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check dual tacho sensors and mechanics, amplifier and related cabling. 
If all signals on one tacho stay low:
- Check tacho sensor power.
Hint: All dual tacho sensor signals toggle between low and high at least once per revolution.
If dual tacho signals fail on both TIUA and TIUB the dual tacho function will be lost. Depending on the installation a speed reduction might be required to protect the installation.

alarms.long_description: Dual tacho quadrature trig count per revolution is wrong.
alarms.cause: Defect wiring, sensors, encoders or sensor support console.\nElectrical noise.
alarms.effect: The controller had to change active tacho encoder set. \nIn case both dual tacho sensor sets are invalid on TIUA and TIUB, dual tacho functionality will be lost. \nEngine speed hunting may occur while the problem is active.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check dual tacho sensors and mechanics, amplifier and related cabling. 
If all signals on one tacho stay low:
- Check tacho sensor power.
Hint: All dual tacho sensor signals toggle between low and high at least once per revolution.
If dual tacho signals fail on both TIUA and TIUB the dual tacho function will be lost. Depending on the installation a speed reduction might be required to protect the installation.
If alarm for low insulation or noise pulse detection have occurred, follow the suggestions action in the alarm text and carefully check cables for wear or damages.

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU*->TIU manager->Dual Tacho->Dual tacho primary/dual speed dev.
alarms.long_description: Dual tacho marker position has slipped.
alarms.cause: The position of dual tacho encoder or the main encoder connected to this TIU has slipped.
alarms.effect: The controller had to change active tacho encoder set. \nIn case both dual tacho sensor sets are invalid on TIUA and TIUB, dual tacho functionality will be lost. \nEngine speed hunting may occur while the problem is active.
alarms.suggested_action:
If alarm for slip for the main encoder (A and B) is observed follow the instructions for that alarm.
If this alarm only occurs on one TIU it is most likely that the mechanical sensor set-up for the dual tacho has slipped. Follow the suggestions below:
- Check the mechanics of the dual tacho installation in general.
- Ensure that no further slipping can occur, and no mechanical parts are loose.
- Monitor regularly the mechanics as slip can cause damage to the engine or the dual tacho installation.
If alarm for low insulation or noise pulse detection have occurred, follow the suggestions action in the alarm text and carefully check cables for wear or damages.

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU->TIU manager->Encoder HW failure
alarms.long_description:
TIUA Controller detected incorrect signals from encoder-A :
Wrong way
Misalignment  of MM & Q1
no encoder data received within expected time frame
alarms.cause:
Possibly Failures:
- Cabling failure (loose connection etc.)
- Defect Digital Input Module
- Encoder failure
- Tacho amplifier A failure
alarms.effect:
CCU and ECU will not use data from TIUA Controller
No redundant reception of engine information (speed, position and direction)

If the other TIU fails, the engine will stop.
alarms.suggested_action:
If the alarm continues to stay active:
- Execute Tacho Commissioning procedure on MOP
check:
- Encoder cables are not broken disconnected (replace Encoder)
- Digital Input Module for correct LED status (replace DI Module)

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU*->TIU manager->Startup position deviation
alarms.long_description: Encoder-A/B power-up position margin too big
alarms.cause: Encoder-A or B marker signals are invalid or encoders are misaligned
alarms.effect: ReducedS accuracy of position estimation. Engine start-up may be impossible
alarms.suggested_action: Turn the engine at least 2 revolutions\nExecute Tacho Commissioning procedure on MOP check:\n- Encoder cables are not broken or disconnected (replace Encoder)

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU*->TIU manager->TIU startup quality
alarms.long_description: TIUA Controller Start up Alarm -TIU quality unknown
alarms.cause: TIUA Controller restarted and position precision is still limited.
alarms.effect: Normal situation after TIUA Controller restart / change of encoder. Alarm must disappear after Air run of approx 3 revolution
alarms.suggested_action:
Air run to ensure evaluation of all encoder signals and alignment of Turning wheel sensor

If the alarm is still active after 3 revolution of Air run:
Go to "Maintenance" -> "Function Test" -> "Tacho"
Follow Tacho test instructions
NOTE: If Encoder A is re-adjusted or replaced:
Perform PMI measurement and restore Tacho offset settings according to 0-diagram

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU*->TIU manager->Missing other TIU telegram
alarms.long_description: Missing network telegram message from the other TIU
alarms.cause: Other TIU node is not transmitting or network connection may be broken. Could also be switch failure or a very fast reduction in engine speed.
alarms.effect: Reduced redundancy. ECS is not able to set Tacho and slip alarms.
alarms.suggested_action:
If the alarm continues to stay active, check:
- TIU node is powered on and LEDs indicates correct status
- Check switch LED status
- Network cabling between the TIU and switch

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU*->TIU manager->Delta TIU A/B error
alarms.long_description: TIUA Controller position margin too big
alarms.cause: The clamping of the Encoder-A or Encoder-B is not reliable
alarms.effect: Engine timing position may not be accurate.\nEngine timing will change if the active TIU is changed leading to max pressure changes
alarms.suggested_action: At first opportunity: Check encoder alignment and fixtures

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU*->TIU manager->Turning wheel sensor slip
alarms.long_description: Misalignment between Turning wheel sensor and encoders
alarms.cause:
a) Failure of Turning wheel sensor signal:
- Cable connection failure
- Sensor failure
- Defect Digital Input Module.
- Physical/mechanical position

b) Failure of Encoder signals:
 - Physical/mechanical position of both encoders has changed (this alarm active on both TIU's)
alarms.effect: If a: CCU and ECU will use data from other TIU if this has a better quality.\n\nIf b: Engine performance will be seriously affected. NEVER ignore this alarm!
alarms.suggested_action:
At first opportunity:
1. Inspect Turning wheel sensor and mounting bracket
2. Check distance between sensor and turning wheel
3. Inspect the mechanical condition of the encoders.
4. Perform tacho test on MOP:
Go to 'Maintenance' -> 'Function Test' -> 'Tacho'
Follow tacho test instructions

NOTE
If it is due to cause b the TWS signal can be invalidated on the 'Maintenance' > 'System View I/O Test' screen. This will disable the supervision and enable the engine to run again. The user take the responsibility manually to check for encoder slip.
If encoder A is readjusted or replaced: Perform PMI measurement, and restore tacho offset settings according to 0-diagram.

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU*->TIU manager->Encoder slip
alarms.long_description: Encoder is out of adjustment/physical placement
alarms.cause: Encoder position signals does not match Turning wheel sensor position
alarms.effect: No redundant reception of engine information (speed, position and direction) CCU Controller and ECU Controller will not use data from TIUA Controller
alarms.suggested_action:
At first opportunity:
1. Inspect physical/mechanical condition of the  Encoder.
2. Re-adjust Encoder
3. Perform Tacho test on MOP
Go to "Maintenance" -> "Function Test" -> "Tacho"
Follow Tacho test instructions

NOTE:
If Encoder A is re-adjusted or replaced: Perform PMI measurement and restore Tacho offset settings according to 0-diagram

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU*->TIU manager->TWS cutout
alarms.long_description: Turning wheel sensor (TWS) is cut-out on MOP
alarms.cause: The user has invalidated the TWS via the "Maintenance>System View I/O Test" screen on MOP A/B
alarms.effect: Encoder A/B slip detection is no longer working. If an encoder slips the engine may be damaged.
alarms.suggested_action:
Invalidating the TWS should only be done if it is related to damaged TWS sensor mount.
The reason for invalidating the TWS signal must be fixed as soon as possible and the TWS signal enabled again.
While the TWS signal is invalidated the user must regular check that no main encoder slip is occurring by:
- Stop the engine and turn it to zero degrees, check that the marking on the turning wheel is at zero degrees
- While the engine is running, monitor the PMI measurements. If any deviation from normal running check with stopped engine must be done.
- If slip occurs for only one encoder, the corresponding TIU should be powered off to force use of the other encoder for engine control.
- If slip is observed for both encoder A and B the engine must be stopped and the encoder installation fixed, to prevent damage to the engine.

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU*->TIU manager->Encoder MM failure
alarms.long_description: Error detected on Marker Master signal
alarms.cause:
- Cabling failure (loose connection etc.), or
 - Turning wheel marker sensor failure, or
 - Encoder failure, or
 - Power failure to Tacho amplifier or
 - Tacho amplifier failure, or
 - Sensor support console failure. 
If trigger ring is fitted, this alarm may be caused by: 
 - Trigger/marker ring is damaged, or 
 - Trigger/marker sensor failure
alarms.effect: The affected encoder will be disabled until the signal is stable for approx 2 revolutions.\n - Redundancy reduced.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check power on the tacho amplifier TSA connector J5 pin (J,A) J=24V A=0V for the affectede encoder.
Trace the error by following the Marker Master signal from :
Encoder and/or turning wheel sensor
->Amplifier (TSA-A)
->TIU 

Perform tacho test on MOP:
 Go to Maintenance -> Function Test -> Tacho
 Follow tacho test instructions

alarms.long_description: Water content in hydraulic oil above high limit XS 1350
alarms.cause: The WIO (water content in hydraulic oil) is above recommended level
alarms.effect: - Can be extremely damaging to engine bearings Particularly valid for Tin-Aluminium lined crosshead bearings.\n- Can be extremely damaging to HCU control valves FIVA / ELFI etc.\n- The higher the water content, the faster the wear rate
alarms.suggested_action:
Check : 
- if salt or freshwater by using cooling water analyse to assist investigation. 
-Investigate and eliminate reason for water to enter the hydraulic oil system . 
- If seawater check : 
- Bellows between engine oil pan outlet and sump tank  
- If seawater supplied oil coolers, check for leakage 
- if fresh water check : n- Engine crankcase for any sign of cooling water leak and compare water level in cooling water expansion tank. 
- Engine top for cooling water presence. Water can run down between cylinder frames. 
- Provided no loss from cooling water expansion tank 
- Check lub oil centrifuges for correct water seal 
- If fresh water cooled lub oil coolers, check for water leakage 
- If steam supplied fire equipment in scavenge space, check for leakage.

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU->IO configuration->DI,4001-B,Encoder MM->4001-B-Encoder MM-Failed Channel
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared 
 (manual re-enabling of an output via the UI on the CPU module or MOP is required :
   1) Check Cabling 
   2) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   3) Replace the corresponding module
   4) Replace CPU module
   5) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU*->IO configuration->DI,4001-B,Encoder MM->4001-B-Encoder MM-Module unavail.
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correctly, or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
1) Check that all modules are inserted correctly.
2) Power cycle the controller.
3) If problems reoccurs:
 a) Replace corresponding Triton module and go to step 2.
 b) Replace CPU module and go to step 2.
 c) Replace Triton Controller Frame.

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU->TIU manager->Encoder HW failure
alarms.long_description:
TIUB Controller detected incorrect signals from encoder-B :
Wrong way
Misalignment  of MM & Q1
no encoder data received within expected time frame
alarms.cause:
Possibly Failures:
- Cabling failure (loose connection etc.)
- Defect Digital Input Module
- Encoder failure
- Tacho amplifier B failure
alarms.effect:
CCU and ECU will not use data from TIUB Controller
No redundant reception of engine information (speed, position and direction)

If the other TIU fails, the engine will stop.
alarms.suggested_action:
If the alarm continues to stay active:
- Execute Tacho Commissioning procedure on MOP
check:
- Encoder cables are not broken disconnected (replace Encoder)
- Digital Input Module for correct LED status (replace DI Module)

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU->Monitoring Signals->JCW Across Engine Press->JCW Across Engine Press Low
alarms.long_description: PT8403 Jacket cooling water pressure across engine is low
alarms.cause: Difference pressure is low
alarms.effect: Insufficient cooling water flow
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check if all the cooling water valves on the engine are in the correct position: inlet/outlet of the liners , Inlet/outlet for the cylinder cover/exhaust valves, Drain valves and etc. 
- Check if all the cooling water valves in the vessels cooling water system is in the correct positions. 
- Have any maintenance been carried out on the engine? please ensure if any orifices have been removed that those have been re-installed.
- Please compare the differential pressure with local pressure gauges.

alarms.data_tree_path: TIU->Monitoring Signals->Exh.Gas BeforeTC->Exh.Gas BeforeTC High
alarms.cause:
-Turbocharger worn or fouled.
- High back pressure.
- High pressure drop across air cooler. 
- Extreme high ambient temperature
alarms.effect: Alarm
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Turbocharger for wear and fouling exhaust gas side (TC rotor wear / Nozzle ring fouling). Air side for fouling (Air filter / compressor).
- Scavenging air cooler water side for calcium build up and air side for fouling. 
- Exhaust gas boiler for blocked pipes and fouling
